```python
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Venue odds keys (odds plan Task 2; Q17): lot, min_order, fee_extras, tick_ladder
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
_KRX_LADDER = [[0, 1], [2000, 5], [5000, 10], [20000, 50], [50000, 100], [200000, 500], [500000, 1000]]


def _odds_venues_doc() -> dict:
    """_venues_doc() with all four odds keys on kis and upbit and none on okx, written out of order on purpose."""
    doc = _venues_doc()
    doc["venues"]["kis"].update(
        tick_ladder={"source": "https://example.invalid/ticks", "effective_from": "2026-10-02",
                     "books": {"US_shares_KIS": [[0, 0.01]], "KRX_stock_book": _KRX_LADDER}},
        lot={"source": "https://example.invalid/kis-lot", "units": {"default": 1, "005930": 1}},
        min_order={"source": "https://example.invalid/kis-min", "quote": {"USD": 0, "KRW": 0}},
        fee_extras={"source": "https://example.invalid/kis-fees", "phi_buy": 0, "phi_sell": 0.0})
    doc["venues"]["upbit"].update(
        lot={"source": _T5_UNVERIFIED, "units": {"default": 1e-8}},
        min_order={"source": _T5_UNVERIFIED, "quote": {"KRW": 5000}},
        fee_extras={"source": _T5_UNVERIFIED, "phi_buy": 12.5, "phi_sell": 0},
        tick_ladder={"source": _T5_UNVERIFIED, "effective_from": "2026-01-01", "books": {"crypto_venue": [[0, 1]]}})
    return doc


def test_venue_odds_keys_parse_to_exact_tuples():
    facts = _facts(_odds_venues_doc())
    kis, upbit, okx = facts.venues["kis"], facts.venues["upbit"], facts.venues["okx"]
    ladder = tuple((float(p), float(t)) for p, t in _KRX_LADDER)
    assert kis.lot == (("005930", 1.0), ("default", 1.0)) and kis.min_order == (("KRW", 0.0), ("USD", 0.0))
    assert kis.fee_extras == (0.0, 0.0)                        # an explicit 0 is a signed value (O11)
    assert kis.tick_ladder == (("KRX_stock_book", "2026-10-02", ladder),
                               ("US_shares_KIS", "2026-10-02", ((0.0, 0.01),)))
    assert kis.odds_sources == (("fee_extras", "https://example.invalid/kis-fees"),
                                ("lot", "https://example.invalid/kis-lot"),
                                ("min_order", "https://example.invalid/kis-min"),
                                ("tick_ladder", "https://example.invalid/ticks"))
    assert upbit.lot == (("default", 1e-8),) and upbit.min_order == (("KRW", 5000.0),)
    assert upbit.fee_extras == (12.5, 0.0) and upbit.tick_ladder == (("crypto_venue", "2026-01-01", ((0.0, 1.0),)),)
    assert upbit.odds_sources == tuple((k, _T5_UNVERIFIED) for k in ("fee_extras", "lot", "min_order", "tick_ladder"))
    numbers = [n for _, n in (*kis.lot, *kis.min_order, *upbit.lot, *upbit.min_order)]
    numbers += [*kis.fee_extras, *upbit.fee_extras] + [x for _, _, rows in kis.tick_ladder for row in rows for x in row]
    assert numbers and all(type(n) is float for n in numbers), numbers        # a YAML int is stored as a float
    assert (okx.lot, okx.min_order, okx.fee_extras, okx.tick_ladder, okx.odds_sources) == ((), (), None, (), ())

    assert upbit.markets == {("BTC", "KRW"), ("USDT", "KRW")} and upbit.default_quote == "KRW"

def test_venue_odds_lookups_fall_back_and_answer_none():
    facts = _facts(_odds_venues_doc())
    kis, upbit, okx = facts.venues["kis"], facts.venues["upbit"], facts.venues["okx"]
    assert kis.lot_for("005930") == 1.0 and kis.lot_for("TQQQ") == 1.0      # TQQQ: the venue's default step
    assert upbit.lot_for("BTC") == upbit.lot_for("XRP") == 1e-8 and okx.lot_for("BTC") is None
    vdoc = _odds_venues_doc()
    vdoc["venues"]["kis"]["lot"]["units"] = {"005930": 10, "AAPL": 0.5}    # no default: every other symbol has none
    narrow = _facts(vdoc).venues["kis"]

    assert kis.min_order_for("KRW") == kis.min_order_for("USD") == 0.0
    assert upbit.min_order_for("KRW") == 5000.0 and upbit.min_order_for("USDT") is None
    assert okx.min_order_for("USDT") is None
    assert kis.ladder_for("KRX_stock_book") == ("2026-10-02", tuple((float(p), float(t)) for p, t in _KRX_LADDER))
    assert kis.ladder_for("US_shares_KIS") == ("2026-10-02", ((0.0, 0.01),))
    assert kis.ladder_for("KRX_ETF_line") is None and upbit.ladder_for("crypto_venue") == ("2026-01-01", ((0.0, 1.0),))
    assert okx.ladder_for("crypto_venue") is None
    for venue in (kis, upbit, okx):
        assert venue.lot_for(None) is None and venue.lot_for(["BTC"]) is None and venue.min_order_for(None) is None
        assert venue.min_order_for(["KRW"]) is None and venue.ladder_for(None) is None


def test_venue_odds_lookups_are_pure_tuple_lookups():
    """lot_for, min_order_for and ladder_for read only the Venue's own tuples: the gate's purity tests scan every
    Venue method (following any module-level def it names) and trap rules.date, rules.Path and rules.os, so no
    parse_date, file, clock or zone name, and no name of a module-level def of rules.py."""
    import ast
    import inspect
    import textwrap
    banned = {"parse_date", "date", "datetime", "Path", "os", "open", "read_bytes", "read_text", "scandir", "now",
              "today", "time", "ZoneInfo", "zoneinfo", "environ", "getenv"}
    defs = {n.name for n in ast.parse(inspect.getsource(rules)).body if isinstance(n, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.ClassDef))}
    for fn in (rules.Venue.lot_for, rules.Venue.min_order_for, rules.Venue.ladder_for):
        tree = ast.parse(textwrap.dedent(inspect.getsource(fn)))
        names = {n.id for n in ast.walk(tree) if isinstance(n, ast.Name)}
        names |= {n.attr for n in ast.walk(tree) if isinstance(n, ast.Attribute)}
        assert names & banned == set(), (fn.__name__, names & banned)
        assert names & defs == set(), (fn.__name__, names & defs)              # the gate's scan follows these
        own = {n.attr for n in ast.walk(tree) if isinstance(n, ast.Attribute)
               and isinstance(n.value, ast.Name) and n.value.id == "self"}
        assert own <= {"lot", "min_order", "tick_ladder"}, (fn.__name__, own)
        assert not any(isinstance(n, (ast.Import, ast.ImportFrom)) for n in ast.walk(tree)), fn.__name__


def test_check_extras_lives_in_the_parser():
    """Spec 4 "Costs": extras may only raise costs. A negative fixed charge makes the venue file, and so the whole
    approved state, INVALID; it never reaches the odds engine (O3)."""
    _need_model()
    vdoc = _odds_venues_doc()
    vdoc["venues"]["upbit"]["fee_extras"]["phi_sell"] = -1
    state = rules.approved_state(_table(_row()), _dump(_map_doc()), _dump(vdoc), seq=1)
    want = "venues: upbit: fee_extras: phi_sell: expected a finite number >= 0, got -1"
    assert not state.valid and state.reason == want, state.reason
    for value in (float("nan"), float("inf"), -float("inf"), -0.5, True, None, "0", [0]):
        _refused(lambda value=value: rules._check_extras({"source": "s", "phi_buy": value, "phi_sell": 0}, "w"),
                 f"w: phi_buy: expected a finite number >= 0, got {value!r}")
    assert rules._check_extras({"source": "s", "phi_buy": 0, "phi_sell": 250}, "w") == (0.0, 250.0)
    _refused(lambda: rules._check_extras({"source": "", "phi_buy": 0, "phi_sell": 0}, "w"),
             "w: source: expected a non-empty string")
    _refused(lambda: rules._odds_number(float("nan"), "w", positive=True), "w: expected a finite number > 0, got nan")
    _refused(lambda: rules._odds_number(0.0, "w", positive=True), "w: expected a finite number > 0, got 0.0")
    assert rules._odds_number(0, "w", positive=False) == 0.0
    assert str(rules._odds_number(-0.0, "w", positive=False)) == "0.0"     # stored unsigned: never shown as -0.0
    assert type(rules._odds_number(3, "w", positive=True)) is float
```

```python
_VENUES_SCHEMA = "tradegen.venues/1"
_VENUE_REQUIRED = frozenset({"sections", "settlement", "source"})
_VENUE_OPTIONAL = frozenset({"markets", "quote_by_currency", "default_quote", "deposits",
                             "lot", "min_order", "fee_extras", "tick_ladder"})      # the odds keys (odds plan Q17)
# The cost books a signed tick ladder may cover. KRX_ETF_line is not one: its ladder is core/quant/instruments.py's.
_LADDER_BOOKS = frozenset({"KRX_stock_book", "US_shares_KIS", "crypto_venue"})


def _odds_number(value, where: str, *, positive: bool) -> float:
    """A finite int or float, never a bool: > 0 when `positive` (as _positive), else >= 0, so that an explicit 0 is
    a signed value. A -0.0 is stored as 0.0 (`+ 0.0`), so a stored value never prints or serialises as -0.0."""
    if positive:
        return _positive(value, where)
    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, (int, float)) or not math.isfinite(value) or value < 0:
        raise Invalid(f"{where}: expected a finite number >= 0, got {value!r}")
    return float(value) + 0.0


def _odds_lot(value, where: str, listed: dict, sections: tuple[str, ...]) -> tuple[tuple[str, float], ...]:
    """`lot: {source, units: {<symbol> | default: step}}` -> sorted (symbol or "default", step > 0); a symbol is one
    the venue's sections list."""
    _keys(value, where, frozenset({"source", "units"}))
    _text(value["source"], f"{where}: source")
    units = value["units"]
    if not isinstance(units, dict) or not units:
        raise Invalid(f"{where}: units: expected a non-empty mapping of symbol (or default) to a step")
    out = []
    for symbol, step in units.items():
        if symbol != "default" and (not isinstance(symbol, str) or symbol not in listed):
            raise Invalid(f"{where}: units: {symbol!r} is not a symbol of sections {list(sections)}")
        out.append((symbol, _odds_number(step, f"{where}: units: {symbol}", positive=True)))
    return tuple(sorted(out))


def _odds_min_order(value, where: str, settlement: frozenset) -> tuple[tuple[str, float], ...]:
    """`min_order: {source, quote: {<settlement asset>: amount}}` -> sorted (asset, minimum >= 0 in quote units)."""
    _keys(value, where, frozenset({"source", "quote"}))
    _text(value["source"], f"{where}: source")
    quote = value["quote"]
    if not isinstance(quote, dict) or not quote:
        raise Invalid(f"{where}: quote: expected a non-empty mapping of settlement asset to a minimum")
    out = []
    for asset, amount in quote.items():
        if not isinstance(asset, str) or asset not in settlement:
            raise Invalid(f"{where}: quote: {asset!r} is not one of the settlement assets {sorted(settlement)}")
        out.append((asset, _odds_number(amount, f"{where}: quote: {asset}", positive=False)))
    return tuple(sorted(out))


def _check_extras(value, where: str) -> tuple[float, float]:
    """Spec 4 "Costs" check_extras, here in the parser: `fee_extras: {source, phi_buy, phi_sell}` -> (phi_buy,
    phi_sell), the fixed KRW charges per buy and per sell. Each is finite and >= 0, so an extra can only raise a
    cost, and a negative one makes the venue file Invalid."""
    _keys(value, where, frozenset({"source", "phi_buy", "phi_sell"}))
    _text(value["source"], f"{where}: source")
    return (_odds_number(value["phi_buy"], f"{where}: phi_buy", positive=False),
            _odds_number(value["phi_sell"], f"{where}: phi_sell", positive=False))


def _odds_ladder(value, where: str, sections: tuple[str, ...], instruments: InstrumentMap) -> tuple:
    """`tick_ladder: {source, effective_from, books: {<cost book>: [[price_from, tick], ...]}}` -> sorted (book,
    effective_from "YYYY-MM-DD", ((price_from, tick), ...)). The first price_from is exactly 0 and they strictly
    increase; every tick is > 0; a book is in _LADDER_BOOKS and is the cost book of a symbol in the venue's
    sections. The date is kept as its checked text, so Venue.ladder_for never parses one."""
    _keys(value, where, frozenset({"source", "effective_from", "books"}))
    _text(value["source"], f"{where}: source")
    start = parse_date(value["effective_from"], f"{where}: effective_from").isoformat()
    books = value["books"]
    if not isinstance(books, dict) or not books:
        raise Invalid(f"{where}: books: expected a non-empty mapping of cost book to [[price_from, tick], ...]")
    used = {inst.cost_book for (section, _), inst in instruments.entries.items() if section in sections}
    out = []
    for book, rows in books.items():
        if book == "KRX_ETF_line":
            raise Invalid(f"{where}: books: KRX_ETF_line: its ladder is core/quant/instruments.py's")
        _member(book, f"{where}: books", _LADDER_BOOKS)
        if book not in used:
            raise Invalid(f"{where}: books: {book} is the cost book of no symbol in sections {list(sections)}")
        if not isinstance(rows, list) or not rows:
            raise Invalid(f"{where}: books: {book}: expected a non-empty list of [price_from, tick] rows")
        ladder: list[tuple[float, float]] = []
        for row in rows:
            if not isinstance(row, list) or len(row) != 2:
                raise Invalid(f"{where}: books: {book}: {row!r} is not a [price_from, tick] row")
            price = _odds_number(row[0], f"{where}: books: {book}: price_from", positive=False)
            tick = _odds_number(row[1], f"{where}: books: {book}: tick", positive=True)
            if not ladder and price != 0:
                raise Invalid(f"{where}: books: {book}: the first price_from must be 0, got {row[0]!r}")
            if ladder and price <= ladder[-1][0]:
                raise Invalid(f"{where}: books: {book}: price_from {row[0]!r} is not above the row before")
            ladder.append((price, tick))
        out.append((book, start, tuple(ladder)))
    return tuple(sorted(out))
```

  New text:

```python
    def quote_for(self, inst: Instrument) -> str:
        """What a buy of `inst` pays with here: its currency, or the venue's default quote."""
        return inst.currency if self.quote_by_currency else self.default_quote

    # The odds lookups are plain tuple reads: the gate's purity tests scan every Venue method (no date, file or clock
    # name here, and no local name that is a module-level def of this file).
    def lot_for(self, symbol: str) -> float | None:
        """The lot step of `symbol` here: its own entry, else the venue's "default", else None (not tradable)."""
        if not isinstance(symbol, str):
            return None
        steps = dict(self.lot)
        return steps.get(symbol, steps.get("default"))

    def min_order_for(self, quote: str) -> float | None:
        """The smallest order paid in `quote` (a settlement asset), in `quote` units, or None (not tradable)."""
        if not isinstance(quote, str):
            return None
        return dict(self.min_order).get(quote)

    def ladder_for(self, book: str) -> tuple[str, tuple[tuple[float, float], ...]] | None:
        """(effective_from "YYYY-MM-DD", ((price_from, tick), ...)) of the signed ladder of cost `book`, or None."""
        for name, start, rows in self.tick_ladder:
            if name == book:
                return start, rows
        return None

class VenueFacts:
```

```python
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Odds plan Task 3 (Q18): the sourced odds values of the shipped venues.yaml. No research source gives a fixed
# charge, an Upbit, OKX or US lot, or a US or OKX minimum, so those stay absent and every leg is not tradable until
# the owner adds them (an explicit 0 included) and approves the venues file (O11; a replay leg needs only the Upbit
# lot, R2-5).
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
_T5_KIS_LOTS = "research_notes/Korean resident trading venue legality/domestic_securities_derivatives.md#L161"
_T5_KIS_TICKS = "https://global.krx.co.kr/contents/GLB/06/0602/0602010201/GLB0602010201T3.jsp"
_T5_UPBIT_MIN = "https://docs.upbit.com/kr/docs/krw-market-info"


def test_shipped_venue_odds_values_are_the_sourced_ones():
    _, _, facts = _t5_shipped()
    v = facts.venues
    kis, upbit = v["kis"], v["upbit"]
    assert kis.odds_sources == (("lot", _T5_KIS_LOTS), ("min_order", _T5_KIS_LOTS),
                                ("tick_ladder", _T5_KIS_TICKS)), kis.odds_sources
    assert kis.lot == (("005930", 1.0), ("069500", 1.0)) and kis.min_order == (("KRW", 0.0),)
    ladder = tuple((float(p), float(t)) for p, t in _KRX_LADDER)
    assert kis.tick_ladder == (("KRX_stock_book", "2026-10-02", ladder),), kis.tick_ladder
    assert upbit.odds_sources == (("min_order", _T5_UPBIT_MIN),) and upbit.min_order == (("KRW", 5000.0),)
    assert upbit.lot == () and upbit.tick_ladder == ()
    for vid, venue in v.items():
        assert venue.fee_extras is None, vid                 # no fixed charge is researched: not tradable (O11)
        if vid not in ("kis", "upbit"):
            assert (venue.lot, venue.min_order, venue.tick_ladder, venue.odds_sources) == ((), (), (), ()), vid
        for key, source in venue.odds_sources:
            assert _t5_ref_ok(source) or source == _T5_UNVERIFIED, (vid, key, source)
    assert kis.lot_for("005930") == kis.lot_for("069500") == 1.0 and kis.lot_for("SPY") is None
    assert kis.min_order_for("KRW") == 0.0 and kis.min_order_for("USD") is None    # a US leg has no signed minimum
    assert upbit.lot_for("BTC") is None and upbit.min_order_for("KRW") == 5000.0
    assert kis.ladder_for("KRX_stock_book") == ("2026-10-02", ladder) and kis.ladder_for("KRX_ETF_line") is None
    # _t5_ref_ok only checks that a cited line exists; pin what the research says for every shipped value
    path, _, anchor = _T5_KIS_LOTS.partition("#")
    lines = (_T5_REPO / path).read_bytes().splitlines()
    stocks, etfs = lines[160].decode("utf-8"), lines[162].decode("utf-8")
    assert anchor == "L161" and stocks.startswith("| KOSPI/KOSDAQ cash stocks"), stocks
    assert f"| {kis.lot_for('005930'):g} share |" in stocks, stocks     # the parsed lot is the one the research gives
    assert etfs.startswith("| Plain 1x ETF/ETN") and f"| {kis.lot_for('069500'):g} unit |" in etfs, etfs
    e2 = (_T5_REPO / "QUANTGEN_techfund_research_bundle" / "QUANTGEN_techfund_research" / "research_notes"
          / "E2_nyse_microstructure_execution.md").read_bytes().decode("utf-8").splitlines()
    bands = e2[307:314]                              # lines 308-314: the seven KRX price bands and their ticks
    nums = [[float(n.replace(",", "")) for n in _t5_re.findall(r"\d[\d,]*", band)] for band in bands]
    research = tuple((0.0 if "| below " in band else n[0], n[-1]) for band, n in zip(bands, nums))
    assert research == ladder and _T5_KIS_TICKS in e2[315], research
    day = _t5_date.fromisoformat(kis.tick_ladder[0][1])        # the parsed effective_from is the research's date
    assert e2[2].startswith(f"As of {day.day} {day:%B %Y}."), e2[2]
    up = (_T5_REPO / "research_notes" / "Korean resident trading venue legality"
          / "crypto_domestic_and_overseas_verification.md").read_bytes().decode("utf-8").splitlines()[20]
    assert f"Upbit {upbit.min_order_for('KRW'):,.0f} KRW minimum is confirmed" in up and _T5_UPBIT_MIN in up, up
    # the header clause of CONTRACT 4.2, word for word, in place of the old "ticks later" clause; line 4 unchanged
    head = _t5_raw("venues").split(b"\nschema:", 1)[0].decode("utf-8")
    flat = " ".join(line.removeprefix("# ") for line in head.splitlines())
    clause = ("The compliance plan writes markets, settlement and deposits only; the odds plan added the sourced "
              "lots, minimums and the KRX stock tick ladder; every other odds value is absent until the owner adds "
              "it, so those legs are not tradable, and this file's sha256 changed, so it needs a new approval.")
    assert clause in flat and "ticks later" not in head and head.endswith(
        "\n# A venue with no deposit entry for a coin credits none, so a withdrawal there fails closed."), head
```

What this task does and why:
- The odds core may reach the disk only through `owner.calendar_in_force` (O1, O6). Spec 6.3 refuses a KRX or US plan
  without a signed calendar, and spec 4 "Calendars" checks the calendar set's hash. Today only `rules._calendar_line`
  (the `--check` line) reads the calendar approval, and it gives four lines, not a sha. After this task
  `owner._calendar_approval(now)` holds that reading, checked the way `load_context` checks the tables: the owner
  state at `now` via `_owner_now`, the approvals stamped by `now` via `_up_to` and `in_force`, the stored copy via
  `store_get`. `calendar_in_force(now)` keeps only its `"ok"` outcome. `_calendar_line` keeps its four exact lines
  by mapping the four outcomes. Q19 records this departure from O3's wording ("refactor `_calendar_line` to call
  it"): the line needs four outcomes and `calendar_in_force` returns two. A test pins, on every calendar case below,
  that `calendar_in_force(now)` is the sha exactly when `_calendar_approval(now)` is `("ok", sha)`.
- `calendar_in_force` is stricter than the old line on one point. It checks the whole owner state, KEY CHANGED
  included, where the old line verified the log alone. `_calendar_line` still asks `ctx.owner.ok` first, so every
  `--check` line stays exactly as it was.
- Spec 7.5 puts each grey leg's warning on the card (O3: "so GREY_LEG never needs gate privates").
  `gate.grey_rows(plan, ctx)` returns the in-force grey row ids of the leg, decided as the cash buy `screen` builds.
  It adds no import to `gate.py`, uses none of the `_T9_FORBIDDEN` names, and its docstring and comments never say
  `datetime` or `ZoneInfo`. So `test_gate_call_graph_has_no_clock_zone_file_or_socket`, which scans the whole gate
  source and its imports, covers it unchanged, and so does `test_purity_no_file_clock_zone_or_network`. In the
  shipped table the only grey row is `KR-OKX-SPOT` (in force from 2026-01-15 up to 2027-02-18; its `auto_off`
  2026-12-03 blocks new exposure but does not end it), so an OKX leg gives `("KR-OKX-SPOT",)` and every other venue
  `()`.
- The odds suite needs full signed temp homes, as `compliance_store` already builds them. The helpers move verbatim
  into `tests/compliance_fixtures.py`, renamed public (Q21), with four new keywords: `venues_raw` (approved instead of
  the shipped venues), `calendar_raw` (a `rules.calendar_stream` blob, approved as kind `calendar`), `limits`
  (a `limit_set`) and `cap` (a `cap_set` of `okx_equity_share`). The new entries come after the old ones, and every
  entry is stamped `2026-10-23T00:00:00Z`, so a limit or cap counts from NOW's date 2026-10-24 (D12). With no keyword,
  the log holds exactly what it held before. `compliance_store` imports `HELD`, `NOW` and `TABLES` back and binds its
  old private names, so no existing test body changes.
- Once public, the helpers are shared by Tasks 13, 16 and 18 and the E1 plan, so the moved copy gets three guards
  (hard rules: never write the real `~/.tradegen/compliance/owner.jsonl`, and never write the repo's trust anchor
  `core/compliance/owner_pubkey.pem` with the test key, whose seed, bytes 0..31, is public). `owner_key`, which
  writes the pem, refuses an `owner.PUBKEY_PATH` that is not inside both `home` and `tempfile.gettempdir()`. The old
  check, inside `home` only, let the caller's choice of `home` decide: `full_home(Path.home())` with `pubkey_at`
  forgotten passed it and wrote the anchor (the repo lies under `Path.home()`), and the rest of the home was then
  signed with no refusal, since a temp `TRADEGEN_HOME` also lies under `Path.home()`. The repo is never inside the
  temp dir, so that call is now refused before the pem is written. `sign`, which every log write goes through,
  refuses a log path that is not inside `tempfile.gettempdir()` before it reads or writes the log. With
  `TRADEGEN_HOME` unset (a direct call outside the harness), `owner.log_path()` is under the real `~/.tradegen`
  (core/isolation.py:108), so it is refused; `owner.log_path()` itself still walks the state root for links first

  guard of its own, because each of its writes goes through one of these: the pem through `owner_key`, every log

```python
# Odds plan Task 4 (Q19, Q21): calendar_in_force and the _calendar_approval it shares with the --check line, and the
# signed-home helpers as public fixtures. Every calendar case also checks that calendar_in_force(now) is the sha
# exactly when _calendar_approval(now) is ("ok", sha) (Q19).
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def _calendar_now(now: _dt.datetime) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """owner._calendar_approval(now), once calendar_in_force(now) is checked to agree with it (Q19)."""
    found = owner._calendar_approval(now)
    assert owner.calendar_in_force(now) == (found[1] if found[0] == "ok" else None), found
    return found


def _fixture_calendar() -> bytes:
    """The calendar stream of the signed temp-dir fixture set; imported here, as tests/compliance_tables.py does, so
    a broken macro module fails only the tests that need it."""
    from tests.macro_m1_calendars import fixture_set
    return rules.calendar_stream(fixture_set().data_dir)


def test_signed_home_helpers_are_the_public_fixtures():
    """Q21: the signed-home helpers live in tests/compliance_fixtures.py and this module's old names are bound to
    them, so these tests run the code the odds suite runs. They write only inside the temp home: approve refuses a
    state root other than its `home`, owner_key a pem and sign an owner log outside the temp dir (so never the
    repo's trust anchor or the real ~/.tradegen), each before writing. Every case stays inside temp homes even if a
    guard were missing."""
    import tempfile
    pairs = ((_pubkey_at, F.pubkey_at), (_owner_key, F.owner_key), (_sign, F.sign), (_approve, F.approve),
             (_other_code, F.other_code), (_full_home, F.full_home), (NOW, F.NOW), (HELD, F.HELD),
             (TABLES, F.TABLES))
    assert all(mine is theirs for mine, theirs in pairs), [mine for mine, theirs in pairs if mine is not theirs]
    assert TABLES == ("rules", "instruments", "venues") and NOW == _dt.datetime(2026, 10, 24, 9, 0, tzinfo=model.KST)
    assert HELD == model.Positions(equity_krw=1_000_000.0, holdings={("upbit", "BTC"): 0.01})
    with F.temp_home() as home, F.temp_home():                          # the state root is another temp home
        _raises(lambda: _approve(home, None, "rules", b"x"), AssertionError)
        assert not owner.home().exists() and not (home / "compliance").exists()
    with F.temp_home() as home, _pubkey_at(home / "k.pem"):
        saved, tempfile.tempdir = tempfile.tempdir, str(home / "elsewhere")  # the pem and the log are outside it
        try:
            _raises(lambda: _owner_key(home), AssertionError)
            _raises(lambda: _sign(None, "approved", {}), AssertionError)
        finally:
            tempfile.tempdir = saved
        assert not (home / "k.pem").exists() and not owner.log_path().exists()


def test_full_home_signs_the_odds_keywords():
    """Q21: full_home approves `venues_raw` instead of the shipped venues and `calendar_raw` as kind calendar, and
    signs `limits` as limit_set and `cap` as cap_set, after the entries it always signed. All are stamped
    2026-10-23T00:00:00Z, so the limits and the cap count from NOW's date on (D12). Without them the log is the
    same as before."""
    venues = F.shipped_bytes("venues") + b"\n# a signed venues version for the odds suite\n"
    stream = _fixture_calendar()
    limits = {"total_loss_floor_krw": 21_000.0, "daily_loss_krw": 5_000.0}
    with F.temp_home() as home, _pubkey_at(home / "owner_pubkey.pem"):
        _full_home(home, venues_raw=venues, calendar_raw=stream, limits=limits, cap=0.10)
        ctx = owner.load_context(NOW, HELD)
        assert ctx.owner.ok and ctx.active.valid and ctx.code_signed, (ctx.owner.reason, ctx.active.reason)
        assert ctx.active.hashes["venues"] == model.sha256_hex(venues) != model.sha256_hex(F.shipped_bytes("venues"))
        assert dict(ctx.owner.limits) == limits and dict(ctx.owner.caps) == {"okx_equity_share": 0.10}, ctx.owner
        assert _calendar_now(NOW) == ("ok", model.sha256_hex(stream))
        kinds = [json.loads(line)["kind"] for line in owner.log_path().read_bytes().splitlines()]
        assert kinds == ["approved"] * 3 + ["code_approved", "age_of_majority", "approved", "limit_set", "cap_set"]
        assert {json.loads(line)["utc"] for line in owner.log_path().read_bytes().splitlines()} == \
            {"2026-10-23T00:00:00Z"}
    with F.temp_home() as home, _pubkey_at(home / "owner_pubkey.pem"):
        _full_home(home)
        ctx = owner.load_context(NOW, HELD)
        kinds = [json.loads(line)["kind"] for line in owner.log_path().read_bytes().splitlines()]
        assert kinds == ["approved"] * 3 + ["code_approved", "age_of_majority"], kinds
        assert dict(ctx.owner.limits) == {} and dict(ctx.owner.caps) == {}, ctx.owner
        assert ctx.active.hashes["venues"] == model.sha256_hex(F.shipped_bytes("venues"))
        assert _calendar_now(NOW) == ("none", "")


def test_calendar_in_force_is_the_sha_of_the_intact_signed_copy():
    """Q19, O6: under an OK owner state the latest calendar approval stamped by `now` is in force while its stored
    copy is intact. The stored folder is the set itself; one changed or missing file there makes it
    ("store", sha), so None."""
    stream = _fixture_calendar()
    sha = model.sha256_hex(stream)
    with F.temp_home() as home, _pubkey_at(home / "owner_pubkey.pem"):
        _full_home(home, calendar_raw=stream)
        assert _calendar_now(NOW) == ("ok", sha) and owner.calendar_in_force(NOW) == sha
        assert _calendar_now(_dt.datetime(2026, 10, 24, 0, 0, tzinfo=_dt.timezone.utc)) == ("ok", sha)   # NOW in UTC
        stored = owner.store_dir() / "calendar" / sha
        assert rules.calendar_sha256(stored) == sha and rules.calendar_stream(stored) == stream
        first = sorted(stored.iterdir())[0]
        first.write_bytes(first.read_bytes() + b"# altered\n")
        assert _calendar_now(NOW) == ("store", sha) and owner.calendar_in_force(NOW) is None
        first.unlink()
        assert _calendar_now(NOW) == ("store", sha)


def test_calendar_in_force_is_none_without_an_ok_owner_log():
    """Q19: no owner key, an internal error, a changed key or a broken log give ("log", ""), so None, even with a
    calendar approval in the log."""
    stream = _fixture_calendar()
    with F.temp_home() as home, _pubkey_at(home / "absent.pem"):
        assert _calendar_now(NOW) == ("log", "")                     # before owner act 1 there is no key at all
    with F.temp_home() as home, _pubkey_at(home / "owner_pubkey.pem"):
        _full_home(home, calendar_raw=stream)
        assert _calendar_now(NOW) == ("ok", model.sha256_hex(stream))

        def boom(*args):
            raise RuntimeError("an internal error")

        saved, owner._owner_now = owner._owner_now, boom
        try:
            assert _calendar_now(NOW) == ("log", "")                 # any error but the ValueError fails closed
        finally:
            owner._owner_now = saved
        row = {"utc": "2026-10-20T00:00:00Z", "channel": "toast", "result": "ok", "code": 3, "due": [],
               "overdue": [], "head_seq": 0, "head_sha256": "", "fingerprint": "SHA256:" + "e" * 64}
        owner.alerts_path().write_bytes(model.canonical_json(row).encode("utf-8") + b"\n")
        assert owner.load_context(NOW, HELD).owner.reason == "KEY CHANGED since 2026-10-20"
        assert _calendar_now(NOW) == ("log", "")
        owner.alerts_path().unlink()
        assert _calendar_now(NOW)[0] == "ok"
        with open(owner.log_path(), "ab") as fh:
            fh.write(b'{"seq": 99}\n')
        assert not owner.load_context(NOW, HELD).owner.ok and _calendar_now(NOW) == ("log", "")


def test_calendar_in_force_counts_only_approvals_stamped_by_now():
    """Q19: with no calendar approval it is ("none", ""); one stamped after `now` counts only from its stamp on
    (load_context's cut-off, _up_to); the latest approval in log order among those stamped by `now` wins."""
    stream = _fixture_calendar()
    sha = model.sha256_hex(stream)
    other = b"holidays_KRX.yaml\0x: 1\n\0"                              # a one-file calendar set
    after = _dt.datetime(2026, 10, 25, 9, 0, tzinfo=model.KST)          # 2026-10-25T00:00:00Z
    with F.temp_home() as home, _pubkey_at(home / "owner_pubkey.pem"):
        key = _full_home(home)
        assert _calendar_now(NOW) == ("none", "") and _calendar_now(after) == ("none", "")
        F.store_blob(home, "calendar", stream,
                     _sign(key, "approved", {"kind": "calendar", "sha256": sha}, "2026-10-25T00:00:00Z"))
        assert _calendar_now(NOW) == ("none", "") and _calendar_now(after) == ("ok", sha)
        newer = _approve(home, key, "calendar", other)                  # later in the log, stamped 2026-10-23
        assert _calendar_now(NOW) == ("ok", newer) and _calendar_now(after) == ("ok", newer)
        assert newer == model.sha256_hex(other) != sha


def test_calendar_in_force_refuses_a_naive_or_out_of_range_now():
    """Q19: a naive `now`, a non-datetime, or one that cannot be converted to UTC or Asia/Seoul is ValueError from
    calendar_in_force and _calendar_approval alike (load_context's checks); nothing else raises."""
    with F.temp_home() as home, _pubkey_at(home / "absent.pem"):
        for now in (_dt.datetime(2026, 10, 24, 9, 0), "2026-10-24", _dt.date(2026, 10, 24), None,
                    _dt.datetime(1, 1, 1, tzinfo=model.KST),
                    _dt.datetime(9999, 12, 31, 23, 59, tzinfo=_dt.timezone.utc)):
            _raises(lambda: owner.calendar_in_force(now), ValueError)
            _raises(lambda: owner._calendar_approval(now), ValueError)
        assert owner.calendar_in_force(NOW) is None


def test_calendar_line_maps_the_shared_calendar_approval():
    """Q19: rules._calendar_line (the --check line) reads owner._calendar_approval at the check's moment and maps its
    four outcomes onto its four lines; under an owner state that is not OK it reads nothing."""
    draft = rules.calendar_sha256(ROOT / "core" / "calendars" / "data")
    other, seen = "a" * 64, []
    cases = ((("log", ""), "calendar: not checked (owner log not usable)"),
             (("none", ""), "calendar: no signed approval, so KRX and US plans are refused (crypto plans only)"),
             (("store", other), f"calendar: the signed version {other[:16]} is missing or altered in the store"),
             (("ok", draft), f"calendar: the draft is the version in force ({draft[:16]})"),
             (("ok", other), f"calendar: the draft {draft[:16]} is not the version in force ({other[:16]}); it counts "
                             "only once signed"))
    saved = owner._calendar_approval
    try:
        for result, line in cases:
            owner._calendar_approval = lambda now, result=result: seen.append(now) or result
            assert rules._calendar_line(F.ctx(), ROOT, NOW) == line, result
        broken = F.ctx(owner=model.OwnerState.broken("bad signature on entry 4"))
        assert rules._calendar_line(broken, ROOT, NOW) == "calendar: not checked (owner log not usable)"
    finally:
        owner._calendar_approval = saved
    assert seen == [NOW] * len(cases), seen
```

```python
class _T10Unreadable:
    """A plan leg whose venue cannot be read: grey_rows answers () instead of raising."""

    @property
    def venue(self):
        raise RuntimeError("an unreadable leg")


def test_grey_rows_names_the_in_force_grey_rows_of_the_leg():
    """Q20: the sorted ids of the venue rows in force on ctx.date (effective_from <= date < effective_until) with
    treatment grey that match the leg as a cash buy. It reads the rows of the state in force, so a row signed grey is
    named too; plan.start, horizon_days and the signed code play no part (screen checks those)."""
    day, c = _T8_DAY, F.ctx()
    okx = _t9_plan("okx", "BTC", c.date, 5)
    assert gate.grey_rows(okx, c) == ("KR-OKX-SPOT",)
    assert gate.grey_rows(_t9_plan("okx", "USDT", c.date, 5), c) == ("KR-OKX-SPOT",)
    for venue, symbol in (("upbit", "BTC"), ("kis", "005930"), ("kis", "069500"), ("kis", "SPY")):
        assert gate.grey_rows(_t9_plan(venue, symbol, c.date, 5), c) == (), (venue, symbol)
    for on, ids in ((day(2026, 1, 14), ()), (day(2026, 1, 15), ("KR-OKX-SPOT",)),
                    (day(2026, 12, 3), ("KR-OKX-SPOT",)),          # auto_off blocks new exposure; still in force
                    (day(2027, 2, 17), ("KR-OKX-SPOT",)), (day(2027, 2, 18), ())):
        assert gate.grey_rows(okx, F.ctx(date=on)) == ids, on
    for odd in (_t9_plan("okx", "BTC", "2026-10-23", 0), _t9_types.SimpleNamespace(leg=okx.leg)):
        assert gate.grey_rows(odd, c) == ("KR-OKX-SPOT",), odd
    assert gate.grey_rows(okx, F.ctx(code_signed=False)) == ("KR-OKX-SPOT",)
    both = _t8_with_rows(F.approved(), {"KR-DOMESTIC-SPOT": {"treatment": "grey",
                                                             "match": _t8_row("KR-OKX-SPOT").match}})
    assert gate.grey_rows(okx, F.ctx(active=both)) == ("KR-DOMESTIC-SPOT", "KR-OKX-SPOT")
    # sorted, not in table order: in kr_rules.yaml KR-OKX-SPOT comes before KR-OKX-P2P
    p2p = _t8_with_rows(F.approved(), {"KR-OKX-P2P": {"treatment": "grey", "match": _t8_row("KR-OKX-SPOT").match}})
    assert gate.grey_rows(okx, F.ctx(active=p2p)) == ("KR-OKX-P2P", "KR-OKX-SPOT")
    kis = _t8_with_rows(F.approved(), {"KR-KIS-KRX-SHARE": {"treatment": "grey"}})
    assert gate.grey_rows(_t9_plan("kis", "005930", c.date, 5), F.ctx(active=kis)) == ("KR-KIS-KRX-SHARE",)


def test_grey_rows_is_empty_when_nothing_can_be_looked_up():
    """Q20: () for a context not from load_context, a broken owner log, an invalid state (a snapshot is for exits
    only), a malformed plan, a venue or symbol the state does not list, and any error reading the plan; it never
    raises. The symbol is looked up as screen() looks up a buy, in the map in force only: one that only an earlier
    approved map knows gives ()."""
    c = F.ctx()
    okx = _t9_plan("okx", "BTC", c.date, 5)
    hand = model.Context(**{f.name: getattr(c, f.name) for f in dataclasses.fields(model.Context)})
    dead = model.ApprovedState.invalid("rules: unapproved")
    for context in (None, "ctx", hand, F.ctx(owner=model.OwnerState.broken("bad signature on entry 4")),
                    F.ctx(active=dead), F.ctx(active=dead, snapshot=F.approved())):
        assert gate.grey_rows(okx, context) == (), context
    for plan in (None, "plan", _t9_types.SimpleNamespace(), _t9_types.SimpleNamespace(leg=None),
                 _t9_types.SimpleNamespace(leg=_T10Unreadable()),
                 _t9_plan("binance", "BTC", c.date, 5), _t9_plan("nowhere", "BTC", c.date, 5),
                 _t9_plan(5, "BTC", c.date, 5), _t9_plan("okx", "NOPE", c.date, 5), _t9_plan("okx", None, c.date, 5),
                 _t9_plan("okx", ["BTC"], c.date, 5), _t9_plan("kis", "BTC", c.date, 5)):
        assert gate.grey_rows(plan, c) == (), plan
    cur = F.approved()
    gone = dataclasses.replace(cur, instruments=dataclasses.replace(cur.instruments, entries={
        k: v for k, v in cur.instruments.entries.items() if k != ("crypto", "BTC")}), history_maps=(cur.instruments,))
    assert gate.grey_rows(okx, F.ctx(active=gone)) == ()               # BTC is in the earlier map only
```

```python
# -- signed temp homes (moved from tests/compliance_store.py by the odds plan, Task 4, Q21) ---------------------
# compliance_store binds its old private names to these, so its tests are unchanged; the odds suite builds the same
# homes. A home is signed with the fixed test key only, inside a temp TRADEGEN_HOME: owner_key refuses a pem and
# sign an owner log outside the temp dir (so never the repo's trust anchor or the real ~/.tradegen), and approve a
# state root outside its `home`, each before it writes. owner is imported inside each helper, as in store_blob, so
# temp_home never depends on owner.py importing.
import datetime as _dt  # noqa: E402
import json as _json  # noqa: E402

from core.compliance import model as _model  # noqa: E402

TABLES = ("rules", "instruments", "venues")
NOW = _dt.datetime(2026, 10, 24, 9, 0, tzinfo=_model.KST)
HELD = _model.Positions(equity_krw=1_000_000.0, holdings={("upbit", "BTC"): 0.01})


@contextlib.contextmanager
def pubkey_at(path: Path):
    """owner.PUBKEY_PATH pointed at `path` for the block, restored afterwards."""
    from core.compliance import owner
    saved = owner.PUBKEY_PATH
    owner.PUBKEY_PATH = path
    try:
        yield path
    finally:
        owner.PUBKEY_PATH = saved


def owner_key(home: Path):
    """The test key, its pem written to owner.PUBKEY_PATH, which must lie inside the temp home `home` and inside the
    temp dir, so the repo's trust anchor is never written, even for a `home` that holds the repo. NotRun PENDING
    without cryptography."""
    from core.compliance import owner
    path = owner.PUBKEY_PATH
    if not (path.is_relative_to(home) and path.resolve().is_relative_to(Path(tempfile.gettempdir()).resolve())):
        raise AssertionError(f"owner_key: {path} is outside the temp home {home}")
    key = test_key()
    write_pubkey(path, key)
    return key


def sign(key, kind: str, data: dict, utc: str = "2026-10-23T00:00:00Z") -> tuple[int, str]:
    """Appends one signed owner entry to the temp home's log; returns its anchor (seq, row_sha256). Refused before
    the owner log is read or written when it is not inside the temp dir, so the real ~/.tradegen is never written."""
    from core.compliance import owner
    path = owner.log_path()
    if not path.resolve().is_relative_to(Path(tempfile.gettempdir()).resolve()):
        raise AssertionError(f"sign: {path} is not inside a temp TRADEGEN_HOME")
    lines = path.read_bytes().splitlines() if path.is_file() else []
    prev = _json.loads(lines[-1])["row_sha256"] if lines else owner.GENESIS_PREV
    line = signed_entry(key, len(lines) + 1, prev, kind, data, utc)
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with open(path, "ab") as fh:
        fh.write(line)
    return len(lines) + 1, _json.loads(line)["row_sha256"]


def approve(home: Path, key, kind: str, raw: bytes) -> str:
    """Signs `approved {kind, sha256}` for `raw` and stores the bytes with that entry as their anchor; refused before
    anything is written when the state root is not the temp home `home`."""
    from core.compliance import owner
    if not owner.home().is_relative_to(home):
        raise AssertionError(f"approve: {owner.home()} is outside the temp home {home}")
    return store_blob(home, kind, raw, sign(key, "approved", {"kind": kind, "sha256": _model.sha256_hex(raw)}))


def other_code(key, utc: str = "2026-10-23T00:00:00Z") -> None:
    """Signs a code_approved that names a hash other than the code on disk."""
    from core.compliance import owner
    files = sorted([list(f) for f in owner.code_files(owner.REPO_ROOT)] + [["core/compliance/zz.py", "0" * 64]])
    sign(key, "code_approved", {"sha256": _model.sha256_hex(_model.canonical_json(files)), "files": files}, utc)


def full_home(home: Path, *, rules_raw: bytes | None = None, venues_raw: bytes | None = None,
              calendar_raw: bytes | None = None, limits: dict | None = None, cap: float | None = None):
    """The test key at owner.PUBKEY_PATH, the three shipped drafts (or `rules_raw`, `venues_raw`) approved and
    stored, the current code hash signed and the owner's age recorded; then, only when given, `calendar_raw` (a
    rules.calendar_stream blob) approved as kind calendar, `limits` signed as limit_set and `cap` as the
    okx_equity_share cap_set. Every entry is stamped 2026-10-23T00:00:00Z, so a limit or cap counts from NOW's date
    on (D12). Returns the key. NotRun PENDING without cryptography."""
    from core.compliance import owner
    key = owner_key(home)
    given = {"rules": rules_raw, "venues": venues_raw}
    for kind in TABLES:
        raw = given.get(kind)
        approve(home, key, kind, raw if raw is not None else shipped_bytes(kind))
    files = [list(f) for f in owner.code_files(owner.REPO_ROOT)]
    sign(key, "code_approved", {"sha256": owner.code_hash(owner.REPO_ROOT), "files": files})
    sign(key, "age_of_majority", {"birth_date": "2000-01-01", "evidence": "test fixture"})
    if calendar_raw is not None:
        approve(home, key, "calendar", calendar_raw)
    if limits is not None:
        sign(key, "limit_set", dict(limits))
    if cap is not None:
        sign(key, "cap_set", {"key": "okx_equity_share", "value": cap})
    return key
```

```python
@contextlib.contextmanager
def _pubkey_at(path: Path):
    """owner.PUBKEY_PATH pointed at `path` for the block, restored afterwards."""
    saved = owner.PUBKEY_PATH
    owner.PUBKEY_PATH = path
    try:
        yield path
    finally:

def _owner_key(home: Path):

    trust anchor is never written. NotRun PENDING without cryptography."""

    """Appends one signed owner entry to the temp home's log; returns its anchor (seq, row_sha256)."""

    prev = json.loads(lines[-1])["row_sha256"] if lines else owner.GENESIS_PREV
    line = F.signed_entry(key, len(lines) + 1, prev, kind, data, utc)
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with open(path, "ab") as fh:

    return len(lines) + 1, json.loads(line)["row_sha256"]


def _approve(home: Path, key, kind: str, raw: bytes) -> str:
    """Signs `approved {kind, sha256}` for `raw` and stores the bytes with that entry as their anchor."""

def _other_code(key, utc: str = "2026-10-23T00:00:00Z") -> None:

    _sign(key, "code_approved", {"sha256": model.sha256_hex(model.canonical_json(files)), "files": files}, utc)


def _full_home(home: Path, *, rules_raw: bytes | None = None):
    """The test key at owner.PUBKEY_PATH, the three shipped drafts (or `rules_raw`) approved and stored, the current
    code hash signed and the owner's age recorded. Returns the key. NotRun PENDING without cryptography."""
```

```python
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# The signed calendar set in force (odds plan Task 4, Q19; spec 4 "Calendars", 6.3; P21, O6)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def _calendar_approval(now: _dt.datetime) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """The latest `approved {kind: calendar}` stamped at or before `now`, read the way load_context reads the
    tables: ("log", "") when the owner state at `now` is not OK (no key, cryptography missing, an unreadable or broken
    log, KEY CHANGED); ("none", "") when no calendar approval is stamped by then; ("store", sha256) when its stored
    copy is missing or altered; ("ok", sha256) otherwise. ValueError for a non-datetime, naive or out-of-range `now`
    (load_context's checks); any other failure is ("log", ""). rules._calendar_line maps the four outcomes onto its
    lines; calendar_in_force keeps "ok" only."""
    if not isinstance(now, _dt.datetime):
        raise ValueError(f"calendar approval: now must be an aware datetime, got {now!r}")
    try:
        now_utc = model.iso_utc(now)                   # ValueError on a naive datetime
        day = now.astimezone(model.KST).date()
    except OverflowError:
        raise ValueError(f"calendar approval: now is out of range, got {now!r}") from None
    try:
        state, check = _owner_now(day, now_utc, None)
        if not state.ok or check is None:
            return "log", ""
        sha = in_force(_up_to(check, now_utc)).get("calendar", ("", 0))[0]
        if not sha:
            return "none", ""
        return ("ok" if store_get("calendar", sha) is not None else "store"), sha
    except Exception:                                  # fail closed: an internal error counts as an unusable log
        return "log", ""


def calendar_in_force(now: _dt.datetime) -> str | None:
    """The sha256 of the calendar set in force at `now` (O6): the latest calendar approval stamped by `now`, under an
    OK owner state, whose stored copy is intact; None otherwise. The odds engine prices a KRX or US leg only when
    this is the sha of the calendar set it was given. Reads the owner log and the store as load_context does;
    ValueError for a non-datetime, naive or out-of-range `now`, and nothing else raises."""
    outcome, sha = _calendar_approval(now)
    return sha if outcome == "ok" else None
```

```python
def _calendar_line(ctx, root: Path, moment) -> str:
    """The calendar draft (P21) against the latest calendar approval signed by `moment` (load_context's cut-off),
    whose stored copy must be intact. The Context does not carry it, so the log is read and verified once more."""
    from core.compliance import model, owner
    if not ctx.owner.ok:
        return "calendar: not checked (owner log not usable)"
    try:
        log = owner.verify_log(owner._log_lines(owner.log_path()), owner.read_pubkey(owner.PUBKEY_PATH),
                               owner.read_anchors())
    except (OSError, ValueError, RuntimeError):         # an unreadable key, anchor or log file means BROKEN (Task 11)
        return "calendar: not checked (owner log not usable)"
    if not log.ok:
        return "calendar: not checked (owner log not usable)"
    signed = owner.in_force(owner._up_to(log, model.iso_utc(moment))).get("calendar", ("", 0))[0]
    if not signed:
        return "calendar: no signed approval, so KRX and US plans are refused (crypto plans only)"
    if owner.store_get("calendar", signed) is None:
        return f"calendar: the signed version {signed[:16]} is missing or altered in the store"
```

```python
def _calendar_line(ctx, root: Path, moment) -> str:
    """The calendar draft (P21) against the latest calendar approval signed by `moment` (load_context's cut-off),
    whose stored copy must be intact. The Context does not carry it, so owner._calendar_approval, which
    owner.calendar_in_force shares (odds plan Q19), reads and verifies the log once more."""
    from core.compliance import model, owner
    if not ctx.owner.ok:
        return "calendar: not checked (owner log not usable)"
    outcome, signed = owner._calendar_approval(moment)
    if outcome == "log":                                # an unreadable key, anchor or log file means BROKEN (Task 11)
        return "calendar: not checked (owner log not usable)"
    if outcome == "none":
        return "calendar: no signed approval, so KRX and US plans are refused (crypto plans only)"
    if outcome == "store":
        return f"calendar: the signed version {signed[:16]} is missing or altered in the store"
```

```python
def grey_rows(plan, ctx) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    """The ids, sorted, of the venue rows in force on ctx.date with treatment grey that match the plan's single leg
    as the cash buy screen() builds (P3: reads plan.leg.venue and plan.leg.symbol only), so the odds engine names a
    plan's grey rows without the gate's private helpers (odds plan Q20). () for a context not from load_context, an
    owner log that is not OK, an unusable state, a venue or symbol the state does not list, or any error. Pure;
    never raises."""
    try:
        leg = getattr(plan, "leg", None)
        venue_id, symbol = getattr(leg, "venue", None), getattr(leg, "symbol", None)
        if not (model.is_sealed(ctx) and ctx.owner.ok and _usable(ctx.active) and _is(venue_id, rules.VENUES)):
            return ()
        state = ctx.active
        venue = state.venues.venues.get(venue_id)
        inst = _lookup(state, venue, symbol, False) if venue is not None else None
        if inst is None:
            return ()
        intent = Intent(venue=venue_id, symbol=symbol, counter_symbol=venue.quote_for(inst), asset=inst.asset,
                        multiple=inst.multiple, action="buy", quantity=1.0, notional_krw=1.0)
        return tuple(sorted(row.id for row in _in_force(state, intent, inst.cls, ctx.date)
                            if row.treatment == "grey"))
    except Exception:
        return ()
```

SHORT_HISTORY below 250 bars), Q24 (codes and their order inside each check), Q25 (field ranges), Q37 (the name and
`detail` never render), Q39 (injected-data checks, STALE_DAYS accepted by R2-8), Q40 (fixtures), Q42 (purity), Q46
item 8 (the start-date, unsigned-code and OKX-cap prechecks and the `stale` and `empty` subs are new refusals);
R2-3 (the leg-count rule below is listed under "For spec rev 3.3"); R2-8; O3-6 (the `series()` default, the
leg-count rule and the plan-file loader contract); R2-13 (this task edits no file of `5816d3c`, so the DRIFT RULE
only covers the names it consumes).

What this task does and why:
- `core/odds/plan.py` is the first module of the signed core. It holds the plan types of spec 7.1, the injected-input
  types the unsigned side fills (CONTRACT 5.2), the nineteen refusal codes of Q24 and the checks that need no prices
  or costs. It imports only `dataclasses`, `hashlib`, `math`, `re`, `collections.abc`, `datetime`, `typing` and
  `core.compliance.model` (and `core.compliance.rules` under `TYPE_CHECKING`, for annotations only), so it passes the
  O1 allowlist, reads no clock, opens no file and adds no other file to the D14 closure.
- Each check returns the first refusal it finds, in the order Q24 fixes, and simulate (Task 13) calls them in that
  order: `check_plan` (step 2), `check_state` (steps 3 and 4), `check_now` (step 5), `check_data` (step 7), then,
  after `costs.terms` and `costs.check_validity` (step 8), `check_history` (step 9).
- `check_plan` follows CONTRACT 5.3. Inside UNSUPPORTED_PRODUCT the rules run in a fixed order: types and ranges
  first (`file`, `track`, `numbers`, `start`, `horizon`, then the leg: `model`, `sizing`, `fraction`, `bracket`,
  `edge`, `replay`), then the venue and the feed, and only on a usable `ctx.active` the instrument rules (`symbol`,
  `feed`, `class`, `multiple`, `tax`). Instrument facts come from the APPROVED map in `ctx.active`, never the draft
  file: a symbol the draft lists but the approved map does not is refused `symbol`. With no usable state the
  instrument rules are skipped and `check_state` refuses STATE_UNUSABLE.
  - The second `feed` rule: the venue parser accepts any of krx, us and crypto as a venue's sections, so an
    owner-signed venue file may give kis the crypto section. Then `kis BTC` finds class `coin`, and Task 13's
    `MARKET[(leg.venue, inst.section)]` would raise KeyError. So a venue and section with no `FEEDS` entry is refused
    `feed` right after `symbol`.
  - Cash and long are structural: a `Leg` has no side, financing or option field. The plan file refuses any other
    key (Task 18), and an option in the approved map derives class `option`, which is refused `class`.
  - The `multiple` rule is defensive: the loader derives `etp_1x`, `share` and `coin` only at +1, so a parsed map
    never reaches it. A hand-built map pins it.
  - Contract 5.3 reads "MULTI_LEG_UNSUPPORTED unless exactly one Leg". Here MULTI_LEG_UNSUPPORTED is returned for two
    or more items, because its catalogue sentence says "more than one leg". An empty list, or one item that is not a
    Leg, is UNSUPPORTED_PRODUCT sub `file`. One Leg in a one-item list or tuple is checked as that leg. RULINGS_ROUND3
    O3-6 adopts this into CONTRACT 3.2, 5.3 and 14.2. Spec 7.1 names MULTI_LEG_UNSUPPORTED with no condition, so
    this rule is also a departure from the spec text: the plan header's "For spec rev 3.3" list carries it, and
    Task 19 folds it into rev 3.3.
  - The three plan numbers must be finite Python floats (sub `numbers`), so `plan_hash` never depends on whether a
    number was typed as `42000` or `42000.0`. `start` must be exactly a `date` (a `datetime` or a date subclass is
    refused) equal to `ctx.date`, which is the gate's own rule in `gate._screen` (`type(start) is model.date`,
    `start != ctx.date`). `horizon_days` must be an int (never a bool) from 1 to 366.
- `check_state` refuses STATE_UNUSABLE for an unsealed context, an owner state that is not OK, or an unusable
  approved state (the gate's `_usable`), with the reason in `detail`; sub `code` when `ctx.code_signed` is not True
  (`screen` would BLOCK it anyway). Then LIMITS_UNSET unless both `LIMIT_KEYS` are present (a floor of 0 is a set
  value), and for an OKX leg sub `cap` unless `ctx.owner.caps.get("okx_equity_share")` passes the gate's `_cap` rule
  (a finite float or an int below 2**63, never a bool, in (0, 1]). It reads the cap with `.get`, so no KeyError.
- `check_now` refuses DATA_INVALID sub `now` unless `now` is an aware datetime whose Asia/Seoul date is `ctx.date`.
  An out-of-range moment (OverflowError) and a tzinfo whose `utcoffset` is not a timedelta (TypeError) are refusals
  too. It runs before the calendar step because `owner.calendar_in_force` raises on a naive `now`.
- `check_data` runs the Q39 rules in the order `series`, `stale`, `sessions`, `empty`, then SYNTHETIC_REFUSED:
  - `series`: an exact `Series`; one length >= 2 for dates, opens and closes; every price > 0 and a finite float or
    an int below 2**63, never a bool (`_real`, the gate's `_number` rule, so a huge int is refused, never converted to
    a float); every date a `YYYY-MM-DD` calendar date (the regex is needed because `date.fromisoformat`
    also takes week dates such as `2025-W52-6`); dates strictly increasing and all before the start; the md5
    recomputed here equal to `series.md5`.
  - `stale`: the last bar more than `STALE_DAYS[market]` calendar days before the start.
  - `sessions`: strictly increasing ISO dates inside `[start, start + horizon_days)`; for KR one price limit in
    (0, 1) per session, for other markets none; a 64-hex lower-case calendar sha for KR and US, `""` for crypto.
  - `empty`: no session at all.
  The core can check only shapes and hashes of what unsigned code passes in; the card says so (Q14).
- `check_history` counts the bars dated before the start. For a KR leg below 60 it is SPECIAL_REGIME (each KIS daily
  row is one KRX session, so gaps only lower the count). Then any leg below 250 is SHORT_HISTORY.
- `plan_hash` is the sha256 of the canonical JSON of the plan with its name blanked, so renaming a plan changes
  nothing (8.o 8). `series_md5` is the md5 of the canonical JSON of the seven series fields (spec 7.2 "Data rules").
- The fixtures follow CONTRACT 3.2, with one change: `series(start=None)` (the contract wrote `start="2024-01-01"`)
  ends the walk on 2026-10-22, the day before `plan()`'s start. With the contract's default, 600 daily bars would
  end on 2025-08-22, and `check_data` would refuse every default series as `stale`. An explicit `start` still
  sets the first date.
  - `ODDS_VENUES` is a complete kis, upbit and okx venue file with every odds key, every source the UNVERIFIED
    literal. It is dumped by PyYAML with no anchors, and Task 2's parser reads it VALID against the shipped
    instrument map.
  - `venues_with` replaces or removes odds keys per venue. A mapping without a `source` gets the UNVERIFIED literal.

```python
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Task 5: fixture venues, series, plans and contexts (contract 3.2). Each function imports core.odds when called,
# so this module still imports where core/odds/plan.py does not exist.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
import copy as _copy  # noqa: E402
import dataclasses as _dataclasses  # noqa: E402
import datetime as _dt  # noqa: E402

import yaml as _yaml  # noqa: E402

_UNVERIFIED = "UNVERIFIED: owner to confirm before approval"
_ODDS_KEYS = ("lot", "min_order", "fee_extras", "tick_ladder")
_LEG_FIELDS = ("venue", "symbol", "model", "bracket", "sizing", "edge_source", "assumed_p")
_KRX_LADDER = [[0, 1], [2000, 5], [5000, 10], [20000, 50], [50000, 100], [200000, 500], [500000, 1000]]


def _zero_extras() -> dict:
    return {"source": _UNVERIFIED, "phi_buy": 0, "phi_sell": 0}


_ODDS_DOC = {"schema": "tradegen.venues/1", "venues": {
    "kis": {"sections": ["krx", "us"], "settlement": ["KRW", "USD"], "quote_by_currency": True, "deposits": [],
            "source": _UNVERIFIED,
            "lot": {"source": _UNVERIFIED, "units": {"005930": 1, "069500": 1, "default": 1}},
            "min_order": {"source": _UNVERIFIED, "quote": {"KRW": 0, "USD": 0}},
            "fee_extras": _zero_extras(),
            "tick_ladder": {"source": _UNVERIFIED, "effective_from": "2026-10-02",
                            "books": {"KRX_stock_book": _KRX_LADDER}}},
    "upbit": {"sections": ["crypto"], "settlement": ["KRW"], "markets": [["BTC", "KRW"], ["USDT", "KRW"]],
              "default_quote": "KRW", "deposits": [{"symbol": "BTC", "network": "bitcoin", "tag_required": False}],
              "source": _UNVERIFIED,
              "lot": {"source": _UNVERIFIED, "units": {"default": 1e-8}},
              "min_order": {"source": _UNVERIFIED, "quote": {"KRW": 5000}},
              "fee_extras": _zero_extras()},
    "okx": {"sections": ["crypto"], "settlement": ["USDT", "USDC"], "markets": [["BTC", "USDT"], ["BTC", "USDC"]],
            "default_quote": "USDT", "deposits": [{"symbol": "BTC", "network": "bitcoin", "tag_required": False}],
            "source": _UNVERIFIED,
            "lot": {"source": _UNVERIFIED, "units": {"default": 1e-8}},
            "min_order": {"source": _UNVERIFIED, "quote": {"USDT": 1}},
            "fee_extras": _zero_extras()}}}


class _NoAliases(_yaml.SafeDumper):
    """A dumper that never writes &anchors or *aliases (the strict loader refuses both)."""

    def ignore_aliases(self, data) -> bool:
        return True


def _dump(doc: dict) -> bytes:
    return _yaml.dump(doc, Dumper=_NoAliases, sort_keys=False, default_flow_style=None, allow_unicode=True,
                      width=1000).encode("utf-8")


ODDS_VENUES: bytes = _dump(_ODDS_DOC)


def venues_with(**changes) -> bytes:
    """ODDS_VENUES with odds keys replaced, per venue: venues_with(upbit={"fee_extras": None, "lot": {"units":
    {"BTC": 1e-4}}}). A mapping replaces the whole key (its "source" defaults to the UNVERIFIED literal); None
    removes the key. Only kis, upbit and okx and the four odds keys can be named (KeyError otherwise)."""
    doc = _copy.deepcopy(_ODDS_DOC)
    for vid, keys in changes.items():
        entry = doc["venues"][vid]
        for key, value in keys.items():
            if key not in _ODDS_KEYS:
                raise KeyError(f"venues_with: {key!r} is not an odds key {_ODDS_KEYS}")
            if value is None:
                entry.pop(key, None)
            else:
                entry[key] = {"source": _UNVERIFIED, **_copy.deepcopy(value)}
    return _dump(doc)


def series(*, symbol="KRW-BTC", source="UPBIT", n=600, seed=1, start=None, vol=0.02, open_gap=0.0,
           price=50_000_000.0, step_days=1):
    """A synthetic random walk as a plan.Series (adjustment "", status "final") with its md5 filled: close-to-close
    log moves N(0, vol); each open is the previous close times exp(open_gap x N(0, 1)), the first one `price`.
    `start` (ISO) is the first date; None ends the series on 2026-10-22, the day before plan()'s start."""
    import numpy as np
    from core.odds import plan as P
    first = (_dt.date(2026, 10, 22) - _dt.timedelta(days=(n - 1) * step_days) if start is None
             else _dt.date.fromisoformat(start))
    dates = tuple((first + _dt.timedelta(days=i * step_days)).isoformat() for i in range(n))
    z = np.random.default_rng(seed).standard_normal((2, n))
    close = price * np.exp(np.cumsum(vol * z[0]))
    open_ = np.concatenate(([price], close[:-1])) * np.exp(open_gap * z[1])
    o, c = tuple(float(x) for x in open_), tuple(float(x) for x in close)
    return P.Series(symbol=symbol, source=source, dates=dates, open=o, close=c, adjustment="", status="final",
                    md5=P.series_md5(symbol, source, dates, o, c, "", "final"))


def plan(**changes):
    """The default plan (contract 3.2): compounding Upbit BTC buy-and-hold, stake KRW 42,000, target KRW 42,000,000,
    fx 1,400.0, start 2026-10-23 (F.ctx's date), horizon 10, bootstrap, fixed(1.0). A Leg field (venue, symbol,
    model, bracket, sizing, edge_source, assumed_p) changes the leg, `leg=` replaces it, any other key changes the
    plan; stake_krw, target_krw and fx_krw_per_usd given as an int become a float."""
    from core.odds import plan as P
    leg_changes = {k: changes.pop(k) for k in _LEG_FIELDS if k in changes}
    leg = changes.pop("leg", P.Leg(venue="upbit", symbol="BTC", model="bootstrap"))
    if leg_changes:
        leg = _dataclasses.replace(leg, **leg_changes)
    fields = dict(name="fixture plan", track="compounding", stake_krw=42_000.0, target_krw=42_000_000.0,
                  fx_krw_per_usd=1_400.0, start=_dt.date(2026, 10, 23), horizon_days=10, fraction=P.fixed(1.0))
    fields.update(changes)
    for key in ("stake_krw", "target_krw", "fx_krw_per_usd"):
        if type(fields[key]) is int:
            fields[key] = float(fields[key])
    return P.Plan(leg=leg, **fields)


def odds_ctx(**overrides):
    """F.ctx with ODDS_VENUES approved and equity KRW 42,000; F.ctx's owner (floor KRW 21,000, daily loss KRW 5,000,
    OKX cap 0.10), signed code and date 2026-10-23 otherwise. Any field can be overridden."""
    from tests import compliance_fixtures as F
    fields = {"active": F.approved(venues=ODDS_VENUES), "equity_krw": 42_000.0}
    fields.update(overrides)
    return F.ctx(**fields)
```

```python
_T5_KRX_DAYS = ("2026-10-23", "2026-10-26", "2026-10-27", "2026-10-28")
_T5_KIS = {"symbol": "005930", "source": "KIS", "price": 70_000.0}
_T5_YAHOO = {"symbol": "AAPL", "source": "YAHOO:AAPL*YAHOO:KRW=X", "price": 300_000.0}


class _T5Date(dt.date):
    """A date subclass: equal to the date it names, but not a plain date."""


class _T5BadTZ(dt.tzinfo):
    """A tzinfo whose utcoffset is not a timedelta, so datetime.utcoffset() raises TypeError."""

    def utcoffset(self, moment):
        return 5


def _t5_code(refusal) -> tuple[str, str] | None:
    return None if refusal is None else (refusal.code, refusal.sub)


def _t5_days(first: dt.date, n: int) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    return tuple((first + dt.timedelta(days=i)).isoformat() for i in range(n))


def _t5_md5(s: P.Series) -> P.Series:
    """`s` with its md5 recomputed (left as it was when a price has no canonical JSON, such as NaN)."""
    try:
        return dataclasses.replace(s, md5=P.series_md5(s.symbol, s.source, s.dates, s.open, s.close, s.adjustment,
                                                         s.status))
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return s


def _t5_series(base: P.Series | None = None, **changes) -> P.Series:
    """`base` (OF.series(n=300) by default) with `changes`; the md5 is recomputed unless `md5` is one of them."""
    s = dataclasses.replace(base if base is not None else OF.series(n=300), **changes)
    return s if "md5" in changes else _t5_md5(s)


def _t5_ending(last: str, n: int = 300, **kwargs) -> P.Series:
    """OF.series of n daily bars whose last bar is dated `last`."""
    first = dt.date.fromisoformat(last) - dt.timedelta(days=n - 1)
    return OF.series(n=n, start=first.isoformat(), **kwargs)


def _t5_inputs(series: P.Series, **changes) -> P.Inputs:
    """Inputs of a 10-day crypto horizon from 2026-10-23 (Task 9 adds the public OF.inputs)."""
    fields = dict(now=_T5_NOW, series=series, sessions=_t5_days(_T5_START, 10), price_limits=(),
                  calendar_sha256="", calendar_version="", calendar_md5s=(), calendar_error="", replay=None,
                  comparison_id="c000001", run_counter=1, comparison_plans=1, comparison_typed=0, plan_runs=1,
                  provenance=P.Provenance(repo_anchor="git:" + "0" * 40, tree_hash="f" * 64, cryptography="49.0.0"))
    fields.update(changes)
    return P.Inputs(**fields)


def _t5_krx(series: P.Series | None = None, **changes) -> P.Inputs:
    """Inputs of a KRX horizon: four sessions, a 30% limit each, a 64-hex calendar sha."""
    fields = {"sessions": _T5_KRX_DAYS, "price_limits": (0.3,) * 4, "calendar_sha256": _T5_SHA, **changes}
    return _t5_inputs(series if series is not None else OF.series(**_T5_KIS), **fields)


def _t5_us(series: P.Series | None = None, **changes) -> P.Inputs:
    """Inputs of a US horizon: two New York sessions, no limits, a 64-hex calendar sha."""
    fields = {"sessions": ("2026-10-23", "2026-10-26"), "calendar_sha256": _T5_SHA, **changes}
    return _t5_inputs(series if series is not None else OF.series(**_T5_YAHOO), **fields)


def _t5_ctx_with(entries: dict) -> model.Context:
    """OF.odds_ctx() whose APPROVED map has `entries` applied ((section, symbol) -> Instrument, or None to drop)."""
    state = F.approved(venues=OF.ODDS_VENUES)
    new = dict(state.instruments.entries)
    for key, inst in entries.items():
        if inst is None:
            del new[key]
        else:
            new[key] = inst
    return OF.odds_ctx(active=dataclasses.replace(state, instruments=dataclasses.replace(state.instruments,
                                                                                          entries=new)))


def _t5_option_ctx() -> model.Context:
    """OF.odds_ctx() whose approved map is the shipped one plus a US option, parsed by the real loader."""
    raw = F.shipped_bytes("instruments")
    assert raw.count(b"\ncrypto:\n") == 1
    entry = (f"  {_T5_OPTION}:\n    asset: us_option\n    multiple: 1.0\n    underlying: null\n    class: option\n"
             "    cost_book: null\n    currency: USD\n    tax_basis: unsupported\n"
             '    source: "fixture: not a real listing"\n').encode("utf-8")
    state = F.approved(instruments=raw.replace(b"\ncrypto:\n", b"\n" + entry + b"crypto:\n"), venues=OF.ODDS_VENUES)
    assert state.valid, state.reason
    assert state.instruments.entries[("us", _T5_OPTION)].cls == "option"
    return OF.odds_ctx(active=state)


def _t5_owner(**changes) -> model.OwnerState:
    return dataclasses.replace(OF.odds_ctx().owner, **changes)

def test_constants_are_the_contracts():
    assert P.REFUSALS == ("PARTIAL_CHUNK", "UNSUPPORTED_PRODUCT", "MULTI_LEG_UNSUPPORTED", "STATE_UNUSABLE",
                          "LIMITS_UNSET", "CALENDAR_UNSIGNED", "CALENDAR_COVERAGE", "DATA_INVALID",
                          "SYNTHETIC_REFUSED", "NOT_TRADABLE", "SPECIAL_REGIME", "SHORT_HISTORY",
                          "CARD_NOT_REPRODUCED", "MODEL_NOT_FOR_LIMITED_VENUE", "COST_DOMINATED", "STUCK_AT_START",
                          "SCREEN_BLOCKED", "ASSUMED_EDGE_UNREACHABLE", "MODEL_CHECK_FAILED")
    assert P.VENUES_OK == ("kis", "upbit", "okx") and set(P.VENUES_OK) <= rules.VENUES
    assert P.CLASSES_OK == ("share", "etp_1x", "coin") and set(P.CLASSES_OK) <= rules.CLASSES
    assert P.TAX_BASES_OK == ("krx_small_holder_exempt", "overseas_22pct_over_2.5m", "crypto_22pct_from_2027")
    assert set(P.TAX_BASES_OK) == rules.TAX_BASES - {"unsupported"}
    assert P.TRACKS == ("moonshot", "compounding") and P.MODELS == ("bootstrap", "garch_t")
    assert P.SIZINGS == ("floor_safe", "stop_based") and P.FRACTION_KINDS == ("fixed", "kelly", "bold")
    assert P.REPLAY_SOURCE == "replay:S_C3_crypto_trend_krwbtc"
    assert P.EDGE_SOURCES == ("none", "assumed", P.REPLAY_SOURCE)
    assert (P.MAX_HORIZON_DAYS, P.MIN_BARS, P.SPECIAL_REGIME_BARS) == (366, 250, 60)
    assert P.STALE_DAYS == {"CRYPTO": 3, "KR": 14, "US": 14}                          # R2-8
    assert P.LIMIT_KEYS == owner._LIMIT_KEYS == ("total_loss_floor_krw", "daily_loss_krw")
    assert P.OKX_CAP_KEY == "okx_equity_share" and P.OKX_CAP_KEY in OF.odds_ctx().owner.caps
    assert P.FEEDS == {("kis", "krx"): "kis_daily", ("kis", "us"): "yfinance", ("upbit", "crypto"): "upbit_daily",
                       ("okx", "crypto"): "binance_x_upbit_usdt"}
    assert P.MARKET == {("kis", "krx"): "KR", ("kis", "us"): "US", ("upbit", "crypto"): "CRYPTO",
                        ("okx", "crypto"): "CRYPTO"}
    assert set(P.MARKET.values()) == set(P.STALE_DAYS) and set(P.MARKET) == set(P.FEEDS)


def test_types_are_frozen_kw_only_dataclasses():
    for cls in (P.Bracket, P.Fraction, P.Leg, P.Plan, P.Refusal, P.Series, P.Provenance, P.ReplayInput, P.Inputs):
        assert dataclasses.is_dataclass(cls) and cls.__dataclass_params__.frozen, cls
        assert all(f.kw_only for f in dataclasses.fields(cls)), cls
    assert P.fixed(1) == P.Fraction(kind="fixed", value=1.0) and type(P.fixed(1).value) is float
    assert P.kelly(0.5) == P.Fraction(kind="kelly", value=0.5) and P.bold() == P.Fraction(kind="bold")
    assert P.bold().value is None
    refusal = P.Refusal(code="LIMITS_UNSET")
    assert (refusal.sub, dict(refusal.slots), refusal.detail) == ("", {}, "")
    leg = P.Leg(venue="upbit", symbol="BTC", model="bootstrap")
    assert (leg.bracket, leg.sizing, leg.edge_source, leg.assumed_p) == (None, "floor_safe", "none", None)
    s = OF.series(n=3)
    assert (s.components, s.proxy_dates) == ((), None)
    try:
        leg.venue = "okx"
    except dataclasses.FrozenInstanceError:
        pass
    else:
        raise AssertionError("Leg is not frozen")


def test_odds_venues_parse_valid_with_every_odds_key():
    state = F.approved(venues=OF.ODDS_VENUES)
    assert state.valid, state.reason
    assert set(state.venues.venues) == {"kis", "upbit", "okx"}
    kis, upbit, okx = (state.venues.venues[v] for v in ("kis", "upbit", "okx"))
    assert kis.lot == (("005930", 1.0), ("069500", 1.0), ("default", 1.0))           # the KRX codes stay text
    assert upbit.lot == okx.lot == (("default", 1e-8),)
    assert (kis.min_order, upbit.min_order, okx.min_order) == ((("KRW", 0.0), ("USD", 0.0)), (("KRW", 5000.0),),
                                                               (("USDT", 1.0),))
    assert (kis.lot_for("005930"), kis.lot_for("069500"), kis.lot_for("AAPL")) == (1.0, 1.0, 1.0)
    assert (kis.min_order_for("KRW"), kis.min_order_for("USD")) == (0.0, 0.0)
    assert kis.fee_extras == upbit.fee_extras == okx.fee_extras == (0.0, 0.0)
    assert kis.ladder_for("KRX_stock_book") == ("2026-10-02", ((0.0, 1.0), (2000.0, 5.0), (5000.0, 10.0),
                                                              (20000.0, 50.0), (50000.0, 100.0), (200000.0, 500.0),
                                                              (500000.0, 1000.0)))
    assert (upbit.lot_for("BTC"), upbit.lot_for("USDT"), upbit.min_order_for("KRW")) == (1e-8, 1e-8, 5000.0)
    assert (okx.lot_for("BTC"), okx.min_order_for("USDT"), okx.min_order_for("USDC")) == (1e-8, 1.0, None)
    assert upbit.ladder_for("crypto_venue") is None and okx.ladder_for("crypto_venue") is None
    assert {key for key, _src in kis.odds_sources} == {"lot", "min_order", "fee_extras", "tick_ladder"}
    assert {key for key, _src in upbit.odds_sources} == {key for key, _src in okx.odds_sources} == {
        "lot", "min_order", "fee_extras"}
    assert {src for v in (kis, upbit, okx) for _key, src in v.odds_sources} == {
        "UNVERIFIED: owner to confirm before approval"}


def test_venues_with_replaces_or_removes_one_venues_odds_keys():
    assert OF.venues_with() == OF.ODDS_VENUES
    raw = OF.venues_with(upbit={"fee_extras": None, "lot": {"units": {"BTC": 0.0001}}})
    state = F.approved(venues=raw)
    assert state.valid, state.reason
    upbit = state.venues.venues["upbit"]
    assert upbit.fee_extras is None and upbit.lot_for("BTC") == 0.0001 and upbit.lot_for("USDT") is None
    assert upbit.min_order_for("KRW") == 5000.0
    assert dict(upbit.odds_sources)["lot"] == "UNVERIFIED: owner to confirm before approval"
    full = F.approved(venues=OF.ODDS_VENUES).venues.venues
    assert state.venues.venues["kis"] == full["kis"] and state.venues.venues["okx"] == full["okx"]
    gone = F.approved(venues=OF.venues_with(kis={"tick_ladder": None})).venues.venues["kis"]
    assert gone.ladder_for("KRX_stock_book") is None and gone.lot_for("005930") == 1.0
    for bad in ({"bithumb": {"lot": None}}, {"upbit": {"markets": None}}):
        try:
            OF.venues_with(**bad)
        except KeyError:
            continue
        raise AssertionError(f"venues_with accepted {bad}")


def test_fixture_defaults_pass_every_check():
    p, ctx = OF.plan(), OF.odds_ctx()
    assert model.is_sealed(ctx) and ctx.date == p.start == _T5_START and ctx.equity_krw == 42_000.0
    assert ctx.code_signed is True and ctx.active.valid
    assert dict(ctx.owner.limits) == {"total_loss_floor_krw": 21_000.0, "daily_loss_krw": 5_000.0}
    assert dict(ctx.owner.caps) == {"okx_equity_share": 0.10}
    assert (p.track, p.stake_krw, p.target_krw, p.fx_krw_per_usd, p.horizon_days) == (
        "compounding", 42_000.0, 42_000_000.0, 1_400.0, 10)
    assert p.leg == P.Leg(venue="upbit", symbol="BTC", model="bootstrap") and p.fraction == P.fixed(1.0)
    s = OF.series()
    assert len(s.dates) == 600 and s.dates[-1] == "2026-10-22" and s.dates[0] == "2025-03-02"
    assert s == OF.series() and s.md5 == _t5_md5(s).md5 and s.status == "final" and s.adjustment == ""
    assert s.open[0] == 50_000_000.0 and s.open[1:] == s.close[:-1]                  # open_gap 0
    assert OF.series(start="2024-01-01", n=3).dates == ("2024-01-01", "2024-01-02", "2024-01-03")
    inputs = _t5_inputs(s)
    assert P.check_plan(p, ctx) is None and P.check_state(p, ctx) is None and P.check_now(ctx, _T5_NOW) is None
    assert P.check_data(p, ctx, inputs, "CRYPTO") is None and P.check_history(p, inputs, "CRYPTO") is None
    widened = OF.plan(stake_krw=50_000, target_krw=60_000, fx_krw_per_usd=1_350)
    assert (widened.stake_krw, widened.target_krw, widened.fx_krw_per_usd) == (50_000.0, 60_000.0, 1_350.0)
    assert all(type(x) is float for x in (widened.stake_krw, widened.target_krw, widened.fx_krw_per_usd))
    assert OF.plan(venue="kis", symbol="005930").leg == P.Leg(venue="kis", symbol="005930", model="bootstrap")
```
