```python
def test_series_labels_components_and_md5_for_krx_and_upbit():
    """The KRX and Upbit legs: symbol, source, adjustment, status, the one component and series_md5 exactly; the
    loader never labels anything synthetic."""
    days = ["2026-10-20", "2026-10-21", "2026-10-22"]
    with _seams(_kis_daily=_kis_fake(_kis_rows(days), [])):
        krx = bars.load_leg(_plan("kis", "005930"), KRX, NOW)
    o, c = (100.0, 101.0, 102.0), (101.0, 102.0, 103.0)
    part = P.series_md5("005930", "KIS", days, o, c, "split", "final")
    assert krx == P.Series(symbol="005930", source="KIS", dates=tuple(days), open=o, close=c, adjustment="split",
                           status="final", md5=P.series_md5("005930", "KIS", days, o, c, "split", "final"),
                           components=(("KIS:005930", part),), proxy_dates=None), krx
    with _seams(_upbit_daily=lambda market, n: _candles(days + ["2026-10-23"], (1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0),
                                                         (1.5, 2.5, 3.5, 4.5))):
        btc = bars.load_leg(_plan("upbit", "BTC"), CRYPTO, NOW)
    o, c = (1.0, 2.0, 3.0), (1.5, 2.5, 3.5)
    md5 = P.series_md5("KRW-BTC", "UPBIT", days, o, c, "", "final")
    assert btc == P.Series(symbol="KRW-BTC", source="UPBIT", dates=tuple(days), open=o, close=c, adjustment="",
                           status="final", md5=md5, components=(("UPBIT:KRW-BTC", md5),), proxy_dates=None), btc
    for s in (krx, btc):
        assert s.status == "final" and "SYNTHETIC" not in s.source.upper(), s


def test_a_failed_feed_raises_and_never_falls_back():
    """Spec 9: SYNTHETIC_REFUSED is never produced by the loader, because it never degrades: a feed that fails
    raises, and nothing is cached. A leg no feed serves (another section, an OKX symbol other than BTC) and a naive
    `now` are refused before any fetch."""
    def down(market, days):
        raise RuntimeError("feed down")
    with _seams(_upbit_daily=down):
        err = _raises(lambda: bars.load_leg(_plan("upbit", "BTC"), CRYPTO, NOW), RuntimeError)
    assert str(err) == "feed down" and not bars.cache_dir().exists(), err
    _raises(lambda: bars.load_leg(_plan("kis", "005930"), types.SimpleNamespace(section="jp"), NOW), ValueError)
    _raises(lambda: bars.load_leg(_plan("okx", "ETH"), CRYPTO, NOW), ValueError)
    _raises(lambda: bars.load_leg(_plan("upbit", "BTC"), CRYPTO, datetime(2026, 10, 23, 9, 0)), ValueError)


def test_us_krw_prices_use_fx_of_the_day_before_for_the_open():
    """O6, Q35: open_KRW = open_USD x FX(d - 1), close_KRW = close_USD x FX(d), FX(x) the close of the last final
    KRW=X bar dated on or before x; a row with no such bar is dropped. At 09:00 KST on 2026-10-23 the NY bar of
    2026-10-22 is final (16:10 EDT = 05:10 KST) and the KRW=X bar of 2026-10-22 is not (00:00Z of 2026-10-24)."""
    us_days = ["2026-10-14", "2026-10-15", "2026-10-16", "2026-10-19", "2026-10-20", "2026-10-21", "2026-10-22"]
    fx_days = ["2026-10-15", "2026-10-16", "2026-10-19", "2026-10-20", "2026-10-21", "2026-10-22"]
    us_o = [600.0 + i for i in range(7)]
    us_c = [601.0 + i for i in range(7)]
    fx_c = {d: 1380.0 + 2 * i for i, d in enumerate(fx_days)}
    calls = []

    def fake(tickers, start, end):
        calls.append((tickers, start, end))
        if tickers == ["SPY"]:
            return _frame("SPY", us_days, us_o, us_c)
        return _frame("KRW=X", fx_days, [v - 1.0 for v in fx_c.values()], list(fx_c.values()))
    with _seams(_yf_download=fake):
        s = bars.load_leg(_plan("kis", "SPY"), US, NOW)
    assert calls == [(["SPY"], START.isoformat(), "2026-10-23"), (["KRW=X"], START.isoformat(), "2026-10-22")], calls
    fx = {"2026-10-15": fx_c["2026-10-15"], "2026-10-16": fx_c["2026-10-16"], "2026-10-18": fx_c["2026-10-16"],
          "2026-10-19": fx_c["2026-10-19"], "2026-10-20": fx_c["2026-10-20"], "2026-10-21": fx_c["2026-10-21"],
          "2026-10-22": fx_c["2026-10-21"]}                          # FX(x): the last final bar on or before x
    keep = [2, 3, 4, 5, 6]                                           # 10-14 and 10-15 have no FX(d - 1)
    before = {"2026-10-16": "2026-10-15", "2026-10-19": "2026-10-18", "2026-10-20": "2026-10-19",
              "2026-10-21": "2026-10-20", "2026-10-22": "2026-10-21"}
    dates = tuple(us_days[i] for i in keep)
    opens = tuple(us_o[i] * fx[before[us_days[i]]] for i in keep)
    closes = tuple(us_c[i] * fx[us_days[i]] for i in keep)
    fx_part = bars.Part(symbol="KRW=X", source="YAHOO", dates=tuple(fx_days[:-1]),
                        open=tuple(fx_c[d] - 1.0 for d in fx_days[:-1]), close=tuple(fx_c[d] for d in fx_days[:-1]),
                        adjustment="")
    us_part = bars.Part(symbol="SPY", source="YAHOO", dates=tuple(us_days), open=tuple(us_o), close=tuple(us_c),
                        adjustment="total")
    assert s == P.Series(symbol="SPY", source="YAHOO:SPY*YAHOO:KRW=X", dates=dates, open=opens, close=closes,
                         adjustment="total", status="final",
                         md5=P.series_md5("SPY", "YAHOO:SPY*YAHOO:KRW=X", dates, opens, closes, "total", "final"),
                         components=(("YAHOO:SPY", bars.part_md5(us_part)), ("YAHOO:KRW=X", bars.part_md5(fx_part))),
                         proxy_dates=None), s


def test_the_okx_composite_uses_krw_usdt_and_krw_x_before_it():
    """O7, Q35: BTCUSDT x KRW-USDT on the same UTC date; before the first KRW-USDT candle, KRW=X with FX(d - 1) and
    FX(d), recorded as proxy_dates; a later date with no KRW-USDT candle is dropped. With KRW-USDT on every date the
    FX feed is never asked (its seam would raise)."""
    btc_days = _dates(date(2026, 10, 10), date(2026, 10, 22))
    usdt_days = [d for d in _dates(date(2026, 10, 15), date(2026, 10, 22)) if d != "2026-10-18"]
    fx_days = _dates(date(2026, 10, 8), date(2026, 10, 22))
    btc_o = {d: 100_000.0 + i for i, d in enumerate(btc_days)}
    btc_c = {d: 100_500.0 + i for i, d in enumerate(btc_days)}
    usdt_o = {d: 1390.0 + i for i, d in enumerate(usdt_days)}
    usdt_c = {d: 1391.0 + i for i, d in enumerate(usdt_days)}
    fx_c = {d: 1370.0 + i for i, d in enumerate(fx_days)}
    asked = []

    def upbit(market, n):
        asked.append(market)
        return _candles(usdt_days, [usdt_o[d] for d in usdt_days], [usdt_c[d] for d in usdt_days])

    def binance(symbol, n):
        asked.append(symbol)
        return _candles(btc_days, [btc_o[d] for d in btc_days], [btc_c[d] for d in btc_days])

    def yf(tickers, start, end):
        asked.append(tickers[0])
        return _frame("KRW=X", fx_days, [v - 1.0 for v in fx_c.values()], list(fx_c.values()))
    with _seams(_upbit_daily=upbit, _binance_daily=binance, _yf_download=yf):
        s = bars.load_leg(_plan("okx", "BTC"), CRYPTO, NOW)
    assert asked == ["BTCUSDT", "KRW-USDT", "KRW=X"], asked
    before = {d: (date.fromisoformat(d) - timedelta(days=1)).isoformat() for d in btc_days}
    want = [(d, btc_o[d] * fx_c[before[d]], btc_c[d] * fx_c[d]) for d in btc_days if d < "2026-10-15"]
    want += [(d, btc_o[d] * usdt_o[d], btc_c[d] * usdt_c[d]) for d in btc_days if d in usdt_o]
    assert s.dates == tuple(w[0] for w in want) and "2026-10-18" not in s.dates, s.dates
    assert s.open == tuple(w[1] for w in want) and s.close == tuple(w[2] for w in want)
    assert (s.symbol, s.source, s.adjustment, s.status) == ("BTC", "BINANCE:BTCUSDT*UPBIT:KRW-USDT", "", "final"), s
    assert s.proxy_dates == ("2026-10-10", "2026-10-14"), s.proxy_dates
    fx_final = [d for d in fx_days if d <= "2026-10-21"]              # KRW=X x is final from 00:00Z of x + 2
    parts = (bars.Part(symbol="BTCUSDT", source="BINANCE", dates=tuple(btc_days), open=tuple(btc_o.values()),
                       close=tuple(btc_c.values()), adjustment=""),
             bars.Part(symbol="KRW-USDT", source="UPBIT", dates=tuple(usdt_days), open=tuple(usdt_o.values()),
                       close=tuple(usdt_c.values()), adjustment=""),
             bars.Part(symbol="KRW=X", source="YAHOO", dates=tuple(fx_final),
                       open=tuple(fx_c[d] - 1.0 for d in fx_final), close=tuple(fx_c[d] for d in fx_final),
                       adjustment=""))
    labels = ("BINANCE:BTCUSDT", "UPBIT:KRW-USDT", "YAHOO:KRW=X")
    assert s.components == tuple(zip(labels, map(bars.part_md5, parts))), s.components
    assert s.md5 == P.series_md5("BTC", s.source, s.dates, s.open, s.close, "", "final"), s.md5
    with _seams(_upbit_daily=lambda m, n: _candles(btc_days, [1.0] * len(btc_days), [2.0] * len(btc_days)),
                _binance_daily=binance):
        full = bars.load_leg(_plan("okx", "BTC", date(2026, 10, 24)), CRYPTO, datetime(2026, 10, 24, 9, 0, tzinfo=KST))
    assert full.proxy_dates is None and [lb for lb, _m in full.components] == ["BINANCE:BTCUSDT", "UPBIT:KRW-USDT"]
    assert full.close == tuple(btc_c[d] * 2.0 for d in btc_days), full.close


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# The cache (Q13, Q36)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def _counting_upbit(calls: list, step: float = 0.0):
    days = _dates(date(2026, 10, 1), date(2026, 10, 22))

    def fake(market, n):
        calls.append(market)
        return _candles(days, [1000.0 + step + i for i in range(len(days))],
                        [1001.0 + step + i for i in range(len(days))])
    return fake


@contextlib.contextmanager
def _cache_off():
    """TRADEGEN_ODDS_BARS_CACHE=0 for the block, the previous value restored afterwards."""
    saved = os.environ.get(bars.CACHE_ENV)
    os.environ[bars.CACHE_ENV] = "0"
    try:
        yield
    finally:
        if saved is None:
            os.environ.pop(bars.CACHE_ENV, None)
        else:
            os.environ[bars.CACHE_ENV] = saved


def test_the_cache_round_trips_and_is_keyed_by_window():
    calls = []
    with _seams(_upbit_daily=_counting_upbit(calls)):
        first = bars.load_leg(_plan("upbit", "BTC"), CRYPTO, NOW)
        again = bars.load_leg(_plan("upbit", "BTC"), CRYPTO, NOW)
    assert first == again and calls == ["KRW-BTC"], calls             # the second load reads the cache
    name = f"UPBIT_KRW-BTC_{START.isoformat()}_{DAY.isoformat()}.json"
    path = bars.cache_dir() / name
    raw = path.read_bytes()
    doc = json.loads(raw)
    assert raw == (model.canonical_json(doc) + "\n").encode("utf-8") and doc["fetched_utc"] == "2026-10-23T00:00:00Z"
    assert doc["dates"] == list(first.dates) and doc["status"] == "final" and doc["adjustment"] == ""
    manifest = (bars.cache_dir() / "MANIFEST.jsonl").read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
    assert manifest == [model.canonical_json({"file": name, "sha256": model.sha256_hex(raw)})], manifest
    assert bars.read_cached("UPBIT", "KRW-BTC", START, DAY).dates == first.dates
    assert bars.read_cached("UPBIT", "KRW-BTC", START + timedelta(days=1), DAY) is None    # another window
    assert bars.read_cached("UPBIT", "KRW-BTC", START, DAY - timedelta(days=1)) is None
    assert bars._cache_name("YAHOO", "KRW=X", START, DAY) == f"YAHOO_KRW=X_{START.isoformat()}_2026-10-23.json"
    assert bars._cache_name("KIS", "A/B C", START, DAY).startswith("KIS_A_B_C_")


def test_the_cache_key_ends_at_the_first_bar_not_yet_final():
    """Q13: a pull made while the 2026-10-22 candle still ran (08:59:59 KST) is keyed by end 2026-10-22, so the run at
    09:00 KST, when that candle is final, fetches again instead of reusing the shorter pull."""
    calls, late = [], datetime(2026, 10, 23, 8, 59, 59, tzinfo=KST)
    with _seams(_upbit_daily=_counting_upbit(calls)):
        early = bars.load_leg(_plan("upbit", "BTC"), CRYPTO, late)
        final = bars.load_leg(_plan("upbit", "BTC"), CRYPTO, NOW)
    assert calls == ["KRW-BTC", "KRW-BTC"], calls
    assert early.dates[-1] == "2026-10-21" and final.dates[-1] == "2026-10-22", (early.dates[-1:], final.dates[-1:])
    for end in ("2026-10-22", "2026-10-23"):
        assert (bars.cache_dir() / f"UPBIT_KRW-BTC_{START.isoformat()}_{end}.json").is_file(), end


def test_an_empty_pull_is_never_cached():
    """yfinance reports a failed download as an empty frame, not an error: such a pull is never pinned, so the next run
    asks again (the core refuses the empty series, DATA_INVALID sub `series`)."""
    with _seams(_yf_download=lambda tickers, start, end: _frame(tickers[0], [], [], [])):
        s = bars.load_leg(_plan("kis", "SPY"), US, NOW)
    assert s.dates == () and not bars.cache_dir().exists(), s


def test_the_cache_fails_closed_on_a_file_that_disagrees_with_its_manifest():
    with _seams(_upbit_daily=_counting_upbit([])):
        bars.load_leg(_plan("upbit", "BTC"), CRYPTO, NOW)
    path = bars.cache_dir() / f"UPBIT_KRW-BTC_{START.isoformat()}_{DAY.isoformat()}.json"
    raw = path.read_bytes()
    path.write_bytes(raw.replace(b'"close":[1001.0', b'"close":[9001.0'))
    err = _raises(lambda: bars.read_cached("UPBIT", "KRW-BTC", START, DAY), RuntimeError)
    assert "sha256 differs" in str(err), err
    _raises(lambda: bars.load_leg(_plan("upbit", "BTC"), CRYPTO, NOW), RuntimeError)   # never refetched silently
    manifest = bars.cache_dir() / "MANIFEST.jsonl"
    manifest.write_text("not json\n", encoding="utf-8")
    _raises(lambda: bars.read_cached("UPBIT", "KRW-BTC", START, DAY), RuntimeError)
    manifest.write_text("", encoding="utf-8")
    assert bars.read_cached("UPBIT", "KRW-BTC", START, DAY) is None    # a file without its line reads as missing


def test_the_cache_fails_closed_on_a_pinned_file_that_is_not_that_part():
    """Q36: a file whose bytes match their manifest line but which is not a final part of the asked source and symbol
    (sorted dates inside the key's window, prices > 0, the source's adjustment) raises; so does another symbol whose
    file name collides ("KRW BTC" and "KRW_BTC" both become KRW_BTC)."""
    good = bars.Part(symbol="KRW-BTC", source="UPBIT", dates=("2026-10-20", "2026-10-21"), open=(1.0, 2.0),
                     close=(1.5, 2.5), adjustment="")
    bars.write_cached(good, START, DAY, NOW)
    assert bars.read_cached("UPBIT", "KRW-BTC", START, DAY) == good
    for bad in (dataclasses.replace(good, status="provisional"), dataclasses.replace(good, dates=good.dates[::-1]),
                dataclasses.replace(good, close=(1.5, -2.5)), dataclasses.replace(good, adjustment="total"),
                dataclasses.replace(good, dates=("2016-10-24", "2026-10-21")),      # before the window start
                dataclasses.replace(good, dates=("2026-10-20", "2026-10-23"))):     # on the key's end
        bars.write_cached(bad, START, DAY, NOW)                        # pinned: its manifest line is the last one
        err = _raises(lambda: bars.read_cached("UPBIT", "KRW-BTC", START, DAY), RuntimeError)
        assert "not a cached part of UPBIT KRW-BTC" in str(err), (bad, err)
    bars.write_cached(dataclasses.replace(good, symbol="KRW BTC"), START, DAY, NOW)
    err = _raises(lambda: bars.read_cached("UPBIT", "KRW_BTC", START, DAY), RuntimeError)
    assert "not a cached part of UPBIT KRW_BTC" in str(err), err


def test_the_cache_is_skipped_when_switched_off_and_on_refetch():
    """TRADEGEN_ODDS_BARS_CACHE=0 skips the write and the read (an existing cache file is not read); refetch skips
    the read and appends a manifest line, which wins from then on."""
    calls = []
    with _cache_off(), _seams(_upbit_daily=_counting_upbit(calls)):
        bars.load_leg(_plan("upbit", "BTC"), CRYPTO, NOW)
        bars.load_leg(_plan("upbit", "BTC"), CRYPTO, NOW)
    assert len(calls) == 2 and not bars.cache_dir().exists(), calls  # neither read nor written
    with _seams(_upbit_daily=_counting_upbit(calls)):
        bars.load_leg(_plan("upbit", "BTC"), CRYPTO, NOW)              # cached now
    with _cache_off(), _seams(_upbit_daily=_counting_upbit(calls, step=7.0)):
        off = bars.load_leg(_plan("upbit", "BTC"), CRYPTO, NOW)        # the cached file is not read
    assert len(calls) == 4 and off.open[0] == 1007.0, (calls, off.open[:1])
    with _seams(_upbit_daily=_counting_upbit(calls, step=5.0)):
        fresh = bars.load_leg(_plan("upbit", "BTC"), CRYPTO, NOW, refetch=True)
    with _seams():
        cached = bars.load_leg(_plan("upbit", "BTC"), CRYPTO, NOW)  # the last manifest line wins; no fetch
    assert len(calls) == 5 and fresh == cached and fresh.open[0] == 1005.0, (calls, fresh.open[:1])
    lines = (bars.cache_dir() / "MANIFEST.jsonl").read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
    assert len(lines) == 2 and json.loads(lines[0])["file"] == json.loads(lines[1])["file"], lines


def test_the_cache_writes_only_through_checked_target():
    """A0: bars.cache_dir() runs state_root()'s link scan first, on a clean temp home (memoised), so the refusal
    below comes from checked_target on the file itself: a hard-linked cache file is never rewritten."""
    base = bars.cache_dir()
    part = bars.Part(symbol="KRW-BTC", source="UPBIT", dates=("2026-10-21",), open=(1.0,), close=(2.0,), adjustment="")
    path = bars.write_cached(part, START, DAY, NOW)
    os.link(path, base / "second_name.json")
    before = path.read_bytes()
    err = _raises(lambda: bars.write_cached(part, START, DAY, NOW), RuntimeError)
    assert "writing it would change another file" in str(err), err
    assert path.read_bytes() == before and not (base / f"{path.name}.tmp").exists()


def test_the_tmp_and_the_manifest_are_checked_too():
    """A0 for the two other targets of write_cached: a hard-linked MANIFEST.jsonl or a hard-linked leftover .tmp is
    refused before anything is written."""
    base = bars.cache_dir()
    part = bars.Part(symbol="KRW-BTC", source="UPBIT", dates=("2026-10-21",), open=(1.0,), close=(2.0,), adjustment="")
    path = bars.write_cached(part, START, DAY, NOW)
    manifest, tmp = base / "MANIFEST.jsonl", base / f"{path.name}.tmp"
    os.link(manifest, base / "manifest_copy.jsonl")
    before = (path.read_bytes(), manifest.read_bytes())
    err = _raises(lambda: bars.write_cached(part, START, DAY, NOW), RuntimeError)
    assert "odds bars MANIFEST" in str(err) and "writing it would change another file" in str(err), err
    os.remove(base / "manifest_copy.jsonl")
    tmp.write_bytes(b"left over")
    os.link(tmp, base / "tmp_copy")
    err = _raises(lambda: bars.write_cached(part, START, DAY, NOW), RuntimeError)
    assert "odds bars cache tmp" in str(err) and "writing it would change another file" in str(err), err
    assert (path.read_bytes(), manifest.read_bytes()) == before and tmp.read_bytes() == b"left over"


def test_the_bars_paths_stay_under_the_tradegen_home():
    """The odds twin of macro_m0_rules.test_every_state_path_stays_out_of_quantgen: with TRADEGEN_HOME unset the
    cache and the yfinance folder resolve under ~/.tradegen and nothing is created; a home inside QUANTGEN is refused
    before any I/O."""
    from core import isolation
    real = Path.home() / ".tradegen"
    existed = (real / "odds").exists()
    saved = os.environ.pop("TRADEGEN_HOME")
    try:
        for p in (bars.cache_dir(), bars.odds_dir() / "yfinance"):
            assert p.resolve().is_relative_to(real.resolve()), p
        os.environ["TRADEGEN_HOME"] = str(isolation.QUANTGEN_STATE / "odds_home")
        _raises(bars.cache_dir, RuntimeError)
    finally:
        os.environ["TRADEGEN_HOME"] = saved
    assert (real / "odds").exists() == existed
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

  Create `core/oddsdata/bars.py` (whole file, LF):

```python
"""Unsigned bar loading for the odds engine (spec 4 "Bars", 7.2 "Price series", "Data rules"; O1, O6, O7, O13; Q6,
Q7, Q13, Q35, Q36).

Outside the D14 closure: `core.oddsdata` is not `core.odds`, so the signed core receives these bars as plain data and
recomputes their md5 itself. Only the four seams reach a data client or yfinance; each imports its client inside and
is looked up at call time, so the odds suite patches them. A bar is kept once it is final (crypto d at 00:00Z of
d + 1, KRX d at 15:40 KST, US d at 16:10 New York time, KRW=X x at 00:00Z of x + 2), and a row whose open or close is
missing, not finite or <= 0 is dropped. Nothing here falls back to synthetic data: a feed that fails raises. Every
downloaded part is cached under state_root()/odds/bars, keyed by (source, symbol, start, end), where end is the first
date of the window that is not final yet, and pinned by its sha256 in MANIFEST.jsonl; TRADEGEN_ODDS_BARS_CACHE=0
turns the cache off."""
from __future__ import annotations

import bisect
import dataclasses
import json
import math
import os
import re
import zoneinfo
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import date, datetime, timedelta, timezone
from pathlib import Path

from core.compliance import model
from core.isolation import checked_target, state_root
from core.odds import plan as P

HISTORY_DAYS = 3650                    # calendar days of history before the plan's start (Q23)
KIS_PAGE = 100                         # rows one KIS daily call returns at most
KIS_MAX_PAGES = 60
FX_TICKER = "KRW=X"                    # Yahoo's KRW per USD (O6; inside the series hash)
ET = zoneinfo.ZoneInfo("America/New_York")      # built once at import; KST is core.compliance.model.KST
_UTC = timezone.utc
CACHE_ENV = "TRADEGEN_ODDS_BARS_CACHE"
_MANIFEST = "MANIFEST.jsonl"
_UNSAFE = re.compile(r"[^A-Za-z0-9.=-]")
_PART_KEYS = frozenset({"symbol", "source", "dates", "open", "close", "adjustment", "status", "fetched_utc"})


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Seams: the only functions that reach a data client or yfinance (looked up at call time)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def _kis_daily(code: str, start: str, end: str) -> list[dict]:
    """KIS daily rows of `code` from `start` to `end` (YYYYMMDD, both included), at most KIS_PAGE, split-adjusted."""
    from data.krx import kis_client
    return kis_client.KISClient().daily(code, start=start, end=end, adjusted=True)


def _upbit_daily(market: str, days: int):
    """The last `days` Upbit daily candles of `market` (a crypto_client.Candles)."""
    from data.crypto import crypto_client
    return crypto_client.UpbitPublic().daily(market, days=days)


def _binance_daily(symbol: str, days: int):
    """The last `days` Binance spot daily klines of `symbol` (a crypto_client.Candles)."""
    from data.crypto import crypto_client
    return crypto_client.BinancePublic().daily(symbol, days=days)


def _yf_download(tickers: list[str], start: str, end: str):
    """yfinance daily bars over [start, end) (yfinance's end is exclusive), total-return adjusted, with its time-zone
    cache moved under the odds folder first (never %LOCALAPPDATA%)."""
    import yfinance
    d = _yf_dir()
    yfinance.set_tz_cache_location(str(d))
    return yfinance.download(tickers, start=start, end=end, auto_adjust=True, progress=False, threads=False,
                             multi_level_index=True)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Paths (resolved at call time, so a test's TRADEGEN_HOME moves them; computing a path creates nothing)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def odds_dir() -> Path:
    return state_root() / "odds"


def cache_dir() -> Path:
    return odds_dir() / "bars"


def _yf_dir() -> Path:
    base = odds_dir()
    d = checked_target(base / "yfinance", "odds yfinance cache", within=base)
    d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    return d


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Finality (Q6, Q35): fixed instants, no data/macro read
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def final_crypto(d: date, now: datetime) -> bool:
    """A crypto daily bar dated d spans 00:00Z of d to 00:00Z of d + 1."""
    return now >= datetime(d.year, d.month, d.day, tzinfo=_UTC) + timedelta(days=1)


def final_krx(d: date, now: datetime) -> bool:
    return now >= datetime(d.year, d.month, d.day, 15, 40, tzinfo=model.KST)


def final_us(d: date, now: datetime) -> bool:
    """New York date d, which closes on the Asia/Seoul date d + 1 in EST and EDT alike."""
    return now >= datetime(d.year, d.month, d.day, 16, 10, tzinfo=ET)


def final_fx(x: date, now: datetime) -> bool:
    """The KRW=X bar's close instant is not published (DIGEST open question 1), so a day of margin."""
    return now >= datetime(x.year, x.month, x.day, tzinfo=_UTC) + timedelta(days=2)


def _final_for(source: str, symbol: str):
    if source == "KIS":
        return final_krx
    if source == "YAHOO":
        return final_fx if symbol == FX_TICKER else final_us
    return final_crypto


def _final_end(start: date, end: date, now: datetime, final) -> date:
    """The end of the final part of [start, end): every date before it is final at `now` (finality is monotone)."""
    while end > start and not final(end - timedelta(days=1), now):
        end -= timedelta(days=1)
    return end


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Parts: one downloaded series each, final rows only
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
@dataclass(frozen=True, kw_only=True)
class Part:
    """One downloaded series in its own quote (KRW for KIS and Upbit, USD for Yahoo, USDT for Binance)."""
    symbol: str
    source: str
    dates: tuple[str, ...]
    open: tuple[float, ...]
    close: tuple[float, ...]
    adjustment: str
    status: str = "final"


def part_md5(part: Part) -> str:
    return P.series_md5(part.symbol, part.source, part.dates, part.open, part.close, part.adjustment, part.status)


def _price(value) -> bool:
    return isinstance(value, (int, float)) and not isinstance(value, bool) and math.isfinite(value) and value > 0


def _iso(text) -> bool:
    try:
        return isinstance(text, str) and date.fromisoformat(text).isoformat() == text
    except ValueError:
        return False


def _ymd(d: date) -> str:
    return d.isoformat().replace("-", "")


def _days_back(start: date, now: datetime) -> int:
    """Upbit and Binance count daily bars back from now: enough to reach `start`, plus one spare."""
    return max(1, (now.astimezone(_UTC).date() - start).days + 2)


def _make_part(symbol: str, source: str, rows, start: date, end: date, adjustment: str) -> Part:
    """The rows dated in [start, end) whose open and close are finite numbers > 0, one per date, sorted."""
    lo, hi, kept = start.isoformat(), end.isoformat(), {}
    for d, o, c in rows:
        if _iso(d) and lo <= d < hi and _price(o) and _price(c):
            kept[d] = (float(o), float(c))
    dates = tuple(sorted(kept))
    return Part(symbol=symbol, source=source, dates=dates, open=tuple(kept[d][0] for d in dates),
                close=tuple(kept[d][1] for d in dates), adjustment=adjustment)


def kis_part(code: str, start: date, end: date, now: datetime) -> Part:
    """KIS daily rows paged backwards, KIS_PAGE a call and at most KIS_MAX_PAGES calls: each call ends the day before
    the earliest row already held, until a short page, a page with no new date, or the window start."""
    end = _final_end(start, end, now, final_krx)
    rows: dict[str, tuple] = {}
    hi = end - timedelta(days=1)
    for _ in range(KIS_MAX_PAGES):
        if hi < start:
            break
        page = list(_kis_daily(code, _ymd(start), _ymd(hi)) or [])
        fresh = [r for r in page if isinstance(r, dict) and _iso(r.get("date")) and r["date"] not in rows]
        for r in fresh:
            rows[r["date"]] = (r.get("open"), r.get("close"))
        if not fresh or len(page) < KIS_PAGE:
            break
        hi = date.fromisoformat(min(r["date"] for r in fresh)) - timedelta(days=1)
    return _make_part(code, "KIS", [(d, o, c) for d, (o, c) in rows.items()], start, end, "split")


def upbit_part(market: str, start: date, end: date, now: datetime) -> Part:
    end = _final_end(start, end, now, final_crypto)
    rows = []
    if end > start:
        candles = _upbit_daily(market, _days_back(start, now))
        rows = list(zip(candles.dates, candles.open, candles.close))
    return _make_part(market, "UPBIT", rows, start, end, "")


def binance_part(symbol: str, start: date, end: date, now: datetime) -> Part:
    end = _final_end(start, end, now, final_crypto)
    rows = []
    if end > start:
        candles = _binance_daily(symbol, _days_back(start, now))
        rows = list(zip(candles.dates, candles.open, candles.close))
    return _make_part(symbol, "BINANCE", rows, start, end, "")


def yahoo_part(ticker: str, start: date, end: date, now: datetime) -> Part:
    end = _final_end(start, end, now, _final_for("YAHOO", ticker))
    rows = _frame_rows(_yf_download([ticker], start.isoformat(), end.isoformat()), ticker) if end > start else []
    return _make_part(ticker, "YAHOO", rows, start, end, "" if ticker == FX_TICKER else "total")


def _frame_rows(frame, ticker: str) -> list[tuple]:
    """(date, open, close) of a yfinance frame with (Price, Ticker) columns; [] when it lacks the ticker."""
    if frame is None or len(frame) == 0:
        return []
    try:
        opens, closes = frame[("Open", ticker)].tolist(), frame[("Close", ticker)].tolist()
    except KeyError:
        return []
    return [(stamp.date().isoformat(), o, c) for stamp, o, c in zip(frame.index, opens, closes)]


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# The bars cache (Q13, Q36): the grokteam write_cached pattern
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def _cache_on() -> bool:
    return os.environ.get(CACHE_ENV, "").strip() != "0"


def _cache_name(source: str, symbol: str, start: date, end: date) -> str:
    return f"{source}_{_UNSAFE.sub('_', symbol)}_{start.isoformat()}_{end.isoformat()}.json"


def _manifest(path: Path) -> dict[str, str]:
    """file name -> sha256, the last line for a name winning; RuntimeError on a line that is not a manifest line."""
    pinned = {}
    for n, line in enumerate(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines(), start=1):
        try:
            row = json.loads(line)
            ok = (isinstance(row, dict) and set(row) == {"file", "sha256"}
                  and all(isinstance(v, str) for v in row.values()))
        except ValueError:
            ok = False
        if not ok:
            raise RuntimeError(f"odds bars cache: {path} line {n} is not a manifest line; delete the bars folder")
        pinned[row["file"]] = row["sha256"]
    return pinned


def _part_from(raw: bytes, source: str, symbol: str, start: date, end: date, name: str) -> Part:
    """The pinned part, refused unless it is a final part of (source, symbol) with the source's adjustment, sorted
    unique ISO dates inside [start, end) and finite prices > 0."""
    lo, hi = start.isoformat(), end.isoformat()
    adjustment = {"KIS": "split", "YAHOO": "" if symbol == FX_TICKER else "total"}.get(source, "")
    try:
        doc = json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"))
        if not isinstance(doc, dict) or set(doc) != _PART_KEYS:
            raise ValueError("not a cached part")
        part = Part(symbol=doc["symbol"], source=doc["source"], dates=tuple(doc["dates"]), open=tuple(doc["open"]),
                    close=tuple(doc["close"]), adjustment=doc["adjustment"], status=doc["status"])
        good = (part.symbol == symbol and part.source == source and part.status == "final"
                and part.adjustment == adjustment and len(part.dates) == len(part.open) == len(part.close)
                and all(_iso(d) and lo <= d < hi for d in part.dates)
                and list(part.dates) == sorted(set(part.dates)) and all(_price(v) for v in part.open + part.close))
    except (UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError, TypeError):
        good = False
    if not good:
        raise RuntimeError(f"odds bars cache {name}: not a cached part of {source} {symbol}; delete it and run again")
    return part


def read_cached(source: str, symbol: str, start: date, end: date) -> Part | None:
    """The cached part of (source, symbol, start, end); None when the cache is off, or the file or its manifest line
    is missing; RuntimeError when the file disagrees with its manifest sha256 or is not that part (fail closed: the
    owner deletes it)."""
    if not _cache_on():
        return None
    base = cache_dir()
    name = _cache_name(source, symbol, start, end)
    path, manifest = base / name, base / _MANIFEST
    if not path.is_file() or not manifest.is_file():
        return None
    pinned = _manifest(manifest).get(name)
    if pinned is None:
        return None
    raw = path.read_bytes()
    if model.sha256_hex(raw) != pinned:
        raise RuntimeError(f"odds bars cache {name}: its sha256 differs from {_MANIFEST}; delete it and run again")
    return _part_from(raw, source, symbol, start, end, name)


def write_cached(part: Part, start: date, end: date, now: datetime) -> Path:
    """Writes `part` as the cache file of (part.source, part.symbol, start, end) and pins its sha256 in the manifest:
    every target checked first (A0), then a tmp file, os.replace, and one appended manifest line."""
    base = cache_dir()
    name = _cache_name(part.source, part.symbol, start, end)
    path = checked_target(base / name, "odds bars cache", within=base)
    tmp = checked_target(base / f"{name}.tmp", "odds bars cache tmp", within=base)
    manifest = checked_target(base / _MANIFEST, "odds bars MANIFEST", within=base)
    raw = (model.canonical_json({**dataclasses.asdict(part), "fetched_utc": model.iso_utc(now)}) + "\n").encode("utf-8")
    base.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    tmp.write_bytes(raw)
    os.replace(tmp, path)
    with open(manifest, "a", encoding="utf-8", newline="\n") as fh:
        fh.write(model.canonical_json({"file": name, "sha256": model.sha256_hex(raw)}) + "\n")
    return path


def _cached_part(fetch, source: str, symbol: str, start: date, end: date, now: datetime, refetch: bool) -> Part:
    """The part from the cache (skipped on refetch), else fetched and, when it holds a row, cached."""
    end = _final_end(start, end, now, _final_for(source, symbol))
    hit = None if refetch else read_cached(source, symbol, start, end)
    if hit is not None:
        return hit
    part = fetch(symbol, start, end, now)
    if part.dates and _cache_on():
        write_cached(part, start, end, now)
    return part


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# The leg's KRW series (Q7, Q35)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def _rows(part: Part):
    return zip(part.dates, part.open, part.close)


def _day_before(d: str) -> str:
    return (date.fromisoformat(d) - timedelta(days=1)).isoformat()


def _fx_at(fx: Part | None, day: str) -> float | None:
    """FX(x): the close of the last final KRW=X bar dated on or before x; None when there is none."""
    i = bisect.bisect_right(fx.dates, day) if fx is not None else 0
    return fx.close[i - 1] if i else None


def _joined(d: str, o: float, c: float, k_open: float | None, k_close: float | None) -> tuple | None:
    if k_open is None or k_close is None or not (_price(o * k_open) and _price(c * k_close)):
        return None
    return d, o * k_open, c * k_close


def _series(symbol: str, source: str, adjustment: str, rows: list, parts: list, proxy=None) -> P.Series:
    dates, opens, closes = (tuple(r[0] for r in rows), tuple(r[1] for r in rows), tuple(r[2] for r in rows))
    return P.Series(symbol=symbol, source=source, dates=dates, open=opens, close=closes, adjustment=adjustment,
                    status="final", md5=P.series_md5(symbol, source, dates, opens, closes, adjustment, "final"),
                    components=tuple((f"{p.source}:{p.symbol}", part_md5(p)) for p in parts), proxy_dates=proxy)


def _okx_btc(get) -> P.Series:
    """BTCUSDT x KRW-USDT on the same UTC date; before the first KRW-USDT candle, KRW=X (FX(d - 1) for the open,
    FX(d) for the close), recorded as proxy_dates. A date after the first KRW-USDT candle without one is dropped."""
    btc, usdt = get(binance_part, "BINANCE", "BTCUSDT"), get(upbit_part, "UPBIT", "KRW-USDT")
    first = usdt.dates[0] if usdt.dates else None
    fx = get(yahoo_part, "YAHOO", FX_TICKER) if any(first is None or d < first for d in btc.dates) else None
    quote = {d: (o, c) for d, o, c in _rows(usdt)}
    rows, proxied = [], []
    for d, o, c in _rows(btc):
        if first is not None and d >= first:
            row = _joined(d, o, c, *quote.get(d, (None, None)))
        else:
            row = _joined(d, o, c, _fx_at(fx, _day_before(d)), _fx_at(fx, d))
            proxied += [d] if row else []
        rows += [row] if row else []
    parts = [btc, usdt] + ([fx] if fx is not None else [])
    return _series("BTC", "BINANCE:BTCUSDT*UPBIT:KRW-USDT", "", rows, parts,
                   (proxied[0], proxied[-1]) if proxied else None)


def load_leg(plan: P.Plan, inst, now: datetime, *, refetch: bool = False) -> P.Series:
    """The KRW series of the plan's leg over [plan.start - HISTORY_DAYS, plan.start), final rows only. `inst` is the
    leg's rules.Instrument from the approved map; ValueError for a leg no feed serves (the core refuses it first)."""
    if not isinstance(now, datetime) or now.utcoffset() is None:
        raise ValueError(f"bars: now must be an aware datetime, got {now!r}")
    leg, end = plan.leg, plan.start
    start = end - timedelta(days=HISTORY_DAYS)

    def get(fetch, source: str, symbol: str) -> Part:
        return _cached_part(fetch, source, symbol, start, end, now, refetch)

    feed = P.FEEDS.get((leg.venue, inst.section))
    if feed == "kis_daily":
        part = get(kis_part, "KIS", leg.symbol)
        return _series(leg.symbol, "KIS", "split", list(_rows(part)), [part])
    if feed == "upbit_daily":
        part = get(upbit_part, "UPBIT", "KRW-" + leg.symbol)
        return _series(part.symbol, "UPBIT", "", list(_rows(part)), [part])
    if feed == "yfinance":
        us, fx = get(yahoo_part, "YAHOO", leg.symbol), get(yahoo_part, "YAHOO", FX_TICKER)
        rows = [_joined(d, o, c, _fx_at(fx, _day_before(d)), _fx_at(fx, d)) for d, o, c in _rows(us)]
        return _series(leg.symbol, f"YAHOO:{leg.symbol}*YAHOO:{FX_TICKER}", "total", [r for r in rows if r], [us, fx])
    if feed == "binance_x_upbit_usdt" and leg.symbol == "BTC":
        return _okx_btc(get)
    raise ValueError(f"bars: no feed serves {leg.venue} {inst.section} {leg.symbol!r}")
```

No existing file is edited, so the DRIFT RULE has nothing to apply here. `tests/odds_acceptance.py` already lists

**Interfaces:**

    approves no calendar by `now`; tests only); `tests.compliance_fixtures`: `NOW` (2026-10-24 09:00 KST), `TABLES`,
    `pubkey_at(path)`, `owner_key(home)`, `approve(home, key, kind, raw)`, `full_home(home, *, rules_raw=None,
    venues_raw=None, calendar_raw=None, limits=None, cap=None)` (every entry stamped 2026-10-23T00:00:00Z; only

  - Task 1: `tests.odds_acceptance._wrap` (hermetic, temp home); `tests.compliance_guards._imports(rel, tree)`.
  - Repo (read-only): `owner.store_dir()` (the approved store; a calendar set is the folder
    `calendar/<sha256>/`); `rules.calendar_sha256(folder)`, `rules.calendar_stream(folder)`, `rules.Invalid`;
    `core.calendars.store.CalendarSet(data_dir)` (`.file(file_id).md5`, `.refusal(file_id)` (loads and caches the

    `CalendarUnsigned`, `CalendarCoverageError`; `core.calendars.clocks.sessions_between(market, lo, hi, *, cal)` and

    originals `core.quant.gate_ledger.repo_anchor`, `UNVERSIONED`, `REPO_ROOT` and
    `core.ficc.macro_artifacts.tree_hash`, `TREE_GLOBS`, `REPO_ROOT` (tests only); `importlib.metadata.version`

- Produces (`core/oddsdata/inputs.py`, contract section 12), for Task 18's CLI:
  - `calendar_for(now) -> tuple[CalendarSet | None, str, str]`: `(set, sha, "")` with the files `sessions` reads
    already loaded, or `(None, "", "unsigned: no signed calendar approval")`, or `(None, "", "unsigned: the stored
    calendar set does not hash to its approval")`;
  - `sessions(market, start, horizon_days, cal) -> (dates, limits, md5s, version, error)` for `market` in KR, US,
    CRYPTO (ValueError otherwise); md5s are `(file id, md5)` pairs in file-id order: KR `holidays_KRX`,
    `kr_regime_tags`, `kr_sessions`; US `holidays_NYSE` (contract 12 names the KR files in another order; that order
    is prose only, and Step 4 records the ruling); error "" | "unsigned: ..." | "coverage: ..." (no dates then);
  - `REPO`, `UNVERSIONED`, `TREE_GLOBS`, `repo_anchor(root=REPO) -> str`, `tree_hash(root=REPO) -> str` (the R2-6
    copies), `provenance() -> plan.Provenance`;
  - `STATE_SCHEMA = "tradegen.odds_state/1"`, `CID_RE = r"c[0-9]{6}"`, `state_path() -> Path`, `begin_run(comparison,
    plan_hashes, typed) -> (cid, run_counter, K, J, R)` with `R: dict[str, int]` keyed by every plan hash passed;
  - `build_inputs(plan, now, *, series, sessions_info, calendar_sha, replay, run) -> plan.Inputs`;
  - module-private: `_MD5_FILES`, `_number`, `_hex64`, `_state_ok`, `_read_state`.

**Plan decisions used:** Q6 (CALENDAR_UNSIGNED and CALENDAR_COVERAGE inputs, the US close on Seoul d + 1), Q12 (the
comparison state; a comparison keeps its own run counter), Q19 (consumed), Q22 (half-open horizon, sessions from the
signed calendar, crypto every date), Q34 (the run counter that enters the seed), Q36 (state format, fail closed);
RULINGS O1, O6, O12; RULINGS_ROUND2 R2-6.

Design notes (read before Step 3):
- `calendar_for` takes the set only through the owner log: `owner.calendar_in_force(now)` names the sha (its store
  check hashes the folder once), the set is read only from `owner.store_dir()/calendar/<sha>`, the four files
  `sessions` reads (`_MD5_FILES`, and the manifest with the first of them) are parsed and cached, and only then is
  the folder hashed again with `rules.calendar_sha256`. So `sessions` uses only bytes that hashed to the approved sha:
  a store copy edited before that second hash is refused, and one edited after it is never read. The shipped
  `core/calendars/data` drafts are never read here. One input is not under the calendar sha: `CalendarSet(folder)`
  takes the `calendars` block of the shipped rules store (`data/macro/rules_v2.0.0.json`: the KR Saturday-session
  cut-off date, the close times), which `tree_hash` records and the owner does not sign. That is part of O1's stated
  limit that the session list is computed by unsigned code.
- `sessions` passes `cal=` on every call and returns "unsigned: no signed calendar set" for a KR or US leg without a
  set, so `core.calendars`' default set (the shipped drafts) is never reached; the test patches
  `store.default`, `clocks.default` and `regime.default` (clocks.py and regime.py bind the name at import) to raise.
- The horizon is half-open, `[start, start + horizon_days)`, so `sessions_between` gets `start + horizon_days - 1`
  as its inclusive end. A US session keeps its New York date; the simulator applies the Asia/Seoul close date d + 1
  (Q22), which the test checks against the fixture calendar's own scheduled closes.
- `repo_anchor` and `tree_hash` are copied verbatim (packed-refs branch included) and pinned by equality tests; this
  file imports neither original (Task 1's `test_oddsdata_never_imports_orders_or_the_study`, and an AST check here).
- `begin_run` validates its arguments and the id before it reads or writes, so an unknown or malformed id, a plan
  hash that is not 64 lowercase hex, or a typed rate that is not a finite number raises ValueError with nothing
  written. A new comparison's id and run counter are both the new `runs` value; an issued id keeps its stored `run`,
  so every invocation of it gives the same market seed (Q12, Q34). The state file is checked in full on read: every
  comparison needs its own `run` with `1 <= run <= runs`, an id equal to `c<run:06d>`, and sorted unique plans and
  rates. That makes every stored id and run unique and no larger than `runs`, so the next new id is never one
  already issued (a hand-lowered `runs` would otherwise merge a "new" comparison into an old one under its seed). A
  file of an earlier layout, a damaged one or a hand-edited one is RuntimeError, never rewritten. The write is
  `checked_target` on the odds folder (within `state_root()`, as `owner._write_new` checks its folder: this refuses an
  odds folder that became a junction after `state_root()`'s once-per-process link scan), then on `state.json` and
  `state.json.tmp` within that folder (contract 12), mkdir, the tmp, then `os.replace`. One writer at a time is
  assumed; the `# ponytail:` comment on `begin_run` names the lock to add if runs can ever overlap, and the c999999
  ceiling of the ids.
- `build_inputs` computes `provenance()` itself (about 0.2 s once the tree is in the OS cache), so every report carries
  the anchor, the tree hash and the cryptography version of the run that made it.
- Budget: the two full temp homes (code hash, signatures, the 17-file calendar store) and the first load of the
  calendar store's config dominate; the module takes about 12 s.

```python
"""Odds plan Task 16: calendar, sessions, provenance and the persisted odds state in core/oddsdata/inputs.py (spec 4
"Calendars", "Provenance", 7.3 "Seeds"; O1, O6, O12; R2-6; Q6, Q12, Q22, Q34, Q36).

Every test runs inside tests.odds_acceptance._wrap (hermetic, a temp TRADEGEN_HOME). Owner logs are built only in
temp homes signed with the fixed test key (tests.compliance_fixtures.full_home). The provenance originals
(core.quant.gate_ledger, core.ficc.macro_artifacts) are imported here, by the tests, never by the module under test."""
from __future__ import annotations

import ast
import contextlib
import dataclasses
import hashlib
import importlib.metadata
import json
import math
import os
import re
from datetime import date, datetime, timedelta
from pathlib import Path

from core import isolation

from core.compliance import model, owner, rules

from core.oddsdata import inputs
from tests import compliance_fixtures as F
from tests import compliance_guards as CG
from tests.macro_m1_calendars import fixture_set

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
KST = model.KST
START = date(2026, 10, 24)                     # F.NOW's Asia/Seoul date, a Saturday
NO_APPROVAL = "unsigned: no signed calendar approval"
ALTERED = "unsigned: the stored calendar set does not hash to its approval"
KRX_30 = ("2026-10-26", "2026-10-27", "2026-10-28", "2026-10-29", "2026-10-30", "2026-11-02", "2026-11-03",
          "2026-11-04", "2026-11-05", "2026-11-06", "2026-11-09", "2026-11-10", "2026-11-11", "2026-11-12",
          "2026-11-13", "2026-11-16", "2026-11-17", "2026-11-18", "2026-11-19", "2026-11-20")
H1, H2, H3 = "1" * 64, "2" * 64, "3" * 64       # plan hashes (64 hex)


def _raises(fn, exc=Exception) -> Exception:
    try:
        fn()
    except exc as e:
        return e
    raise AssertionError(f"expected {exc.__name__}")


def _stream(folder: Path) -> bytes:
    return rules.calendar_stream(folder)


@contextlib.contextmanager
def _home(calendar_raw: bytes | None = None, *, signed: bool = True):
    """A fresh temp home: with signed=True the test key's owner log approves the shipped tables, signs the code hash
    and, when given, approves `calendar_raw` as the calendar set (all stamped 2026-10-23T00:00:00Z); with
    signed=False nothing is signed at all."""
    with F.temp_home() as home, F.pubkey_at(home / "owner_pubkey.pem"):
        if signed:
            F.full_home(home, calendar_raw=calendar_raw)
        yield home


def _plan() -> P.Plan:
    return P.Plan(name="inputs test", track="compounding", stake_krw=42_000.0, target_krw=42_000_000.0,
                  fx_krw_per_usd=1_400.0, start=START, horizon_days=30,
                  leg=P.Leg(venue="upbit", symbol="BTC", model="bootstrap"), fraction=P.fixed(1.0))


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# The calendar set (O6, Q6) and the sessions (Q22)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def test_calendar_for_takes_only_an_owner_approved_set_from_the_store():
    """CALENDAR_UNSIGNED's inputs: with nothing signed, and with a verified owner log that approves the tables but no
    calendar (`_calendar_approval` says "none", not "log"), there is no set. A set already in the store whose
    approval is not yet in force is the NOW - 2 days check of the next test. The shipped drafts approved by the owner
    do give a set, but no session: their own files are unsigned."""
    shipped = _stream(ROOT / "core" / "calendars" / "data")
    with _home(signed=False):
        assert inputs.calendar_for(F.NOW) == (None, "", NO_APPROVAL)
    with F.temp_home() as home, F.pubkey_at(home / "owner_pubkey.pem"):
        key = F.owner_key(home)                                       # a verified log that approves no calendar
        for kind in F.TABLES:
            F.approve(home, key, kind, F.shipped_bytes(kind))
        assert owner._calendar_approval(F.NOW) == ("none", ""), owner._calendar_approval(F.NOW)
        assert inputs.calendar_for(F.NOW) == (None, "", NO_APPROVAL)
    with _home(shipped):
        cal, sha, err = inputs.calendar_for(F.NOW)
        assert cal is not None and sha == model.sha256_hex(shipped) and err == "", (sha, err)
        for market in ("KR", "US"):
            got = inputs.sessions(market, START, 30, cal)
            assert got[:4] == ((), (), (), "") and got[4].startswith("unsigned: "), (market, got)


def test_the_approved_fixture_set_gives_sessions_limits_and_md5s():
    """One full temp home approves fixture_set(). The set comes from the store under the sha calendar_in_force
    names, with the files sessions() reads already loaded: a stored copy overwritten right after calendar_for
    returned never reaches sessions(). With core.calendars' three `default` functions patched to raise (clocks.py and
    regime.py bind the name at import), every call passes cal=: KRX sessions of [2026-10-24, 2026-11-23) with the
    dated price limit 0.30 and the three KR md5s; US sessions whose scheduled closes (EDT, EST, the 13:00 early close
    of 2026-11-27) fall on the Asia/Seoul date d + 1; a horizon past 2027-12-31 gives "coverage: ..." and the last
    one inside it passes. The next calendar_for refuses the edited copy, and so does one whose calendar_in_force
    check came before the edit."""
    from core.calendars import regime, store
    fixture = _stream(fixture_set().data_dir)
    sha = model.sha256_hex(fixture)
    ref = fixture_set()

    def boom():
        raise AssertionError("a core.calendars default() was called")
    with _home(fixture):
        cal, got_sha, err = inputs.calendar_for(F.NOW)
        assert got_sha == sha == owner.calendar_in_force(F.NOW) and err == "", (got_sha, err)
        assert isinstance(cal, CalendarSet) and cal.data_dir == owner.store_dir() / "calendar" / sha, cal
        assert inputs.calendar_for(F.NOW - timedelta(days=2)) == (None, "", NO_APPROVAL)   # before it was signed
        _raises(lambda: inputs.calendar_for(datetime(2026, 10, 24, 9, 0)), ValueError)   # naive
        stored = cal.data_dir / "holidays_KRX.yaml"
        approved = stored.read_bytes()
        stored.write_bytes(b"\xff not the approved file\n")          # after calendar_for: sessions() never reads it
        saved = (store.default, clocks.default, regime.default)
        store.default = clocks.default = regime.default = boom
        try:
            kr = inputs.sessions("KR", START, 30, cal)
            us = inputs.sessions("US", START, 60, cal)
            closes = {d: clocks.decision_time_utc("US", date.fromisoformat(d), cal=cal) for d in us[0]}
            late = {m: inputs.sessions(m, date(2027, 12, 20), 30, cal) for m in ("KR", "US")}
            last = {m: inputs.sessions(m, date(2027, 12, 2), 30, cal) for m in ("KR", "US")}   # [12-02, 2028-01-01)
        finally:
            store.default, clocks.default, regime.default = saved
        assert inputs.calendar_for(F.NOW) == (None, "", NO_APPROVAL)         # calendar_in_force sees the edit
        stored.write_bytes(approved + b"# edited after approval\n")
        keep = owner.calendar_in_force
        owner.calendar_in_force = lambda now: sha                            # an edit after that check
        try:
            assert inputs.calendar_for(F.NOW) == (None, "", ALTERED)
        finally:
            owner.calendar_in_force = keep
    dates, limits, md5s, version, error = kr
    assert (dates, limits, version, error) == (KRX_30, (0.30,) * 20, "1.0.0-fixture", ""), kr
    closed = ref.holiday_set("KRX")[0]
    assert dates == tuple(d.isoformat() for d in (START + timedelta(days=i) for i in range(30))
                          if d.weekday() < 5 and d not in closed)
    assert md5s == tuple((fid, ref.file(fid).md5) for fid in ("holidays_KRX", "kr_regime_tags", "kr_sessions")), md5s
    assert all(re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{32}", m) for _fid, m in md5s), md5s
    dates, limits, md5s, version, error = us
    assert (len(dates), dates[0], dates[-1]) == (41, "2026-10-26", "2026-12-22") and "2026-11-26" not in dates, us
    assert (limits, md5s, version, error) == ((), (("holidays_NYSE", ref.file("holidays_NYSE").md5),),
                                              "1.0.0-fixture", ""), us
    for d, close in closes.items():
        assert close.astimezone(KST).date() == date.fromisoformat(d) + timedelta(days=1), (d, close)
    assert date(2026, 11, 27) in ref.holiday_set("NYSE")[1] and "2026-11-27" in dates
    assert [closes[d].astimezone(KST).hour for d in ("2026-10-26", "2026-11-02", "2026-11-27")] == [5, 6, 3]
    for market in ("KR", "US"):
        got, ok = late[market], last[market]
        assert got[:4] == ((), (), (), "") and got[4].startswith("coverage: ") and "2028-01-01" in got[4], got
        assert ok[4] == "" and ok[0] and ok[0][-1] <= "2027-12-31", (market, ok)


def test_crypto_sessions_and_a_missing_calendar():
    """Crypto: every date of the half-open horizon, no calendar. A KR or US leg without a set is "unsigned: ..."
    (never core.calendars' default set); any other market is a ValueError."""
    assert inputs.sessions("CRYPTO", START, 3, None) == (("2026-10-24", "2026-10-25", "2026-10-26"), (), (), "", "")
    assert len(inputs.sessions("CRYPTO", START, 366, None)[0]) == 366
    for market in ("KR", "US"):
        assert inputs.sessions(market, START, 30, None) == ((), (), (), "", "unsigned: no signed calendar set")
    _raises(lambda: inputs.sessions("JP", START, 30, None), ValueError)

def test_provenance_strings_and_versions():
    p = inputs.provenance()
    assert re.fullmatch(r"git:[0-9a-f]{40}", p.repo_anchor) or p.repo_anchor == "UNVERSIONED", p
    assert re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{64}", p.tree_hash), p
    assert p.cryptography == importlib.metadata.version("cryptography"), p
    saved = importlib.metadata.version

    def missing(name):
        raise importlib.metadata.PackageNotFoundError(name)
    importlib.metadata.version = missing
    try:
        assert inputs.provenance().cryptography == "absent"
    finally:
        importlib.metadata.version = saved


def test_the_provenance_copies_equal_the_originals_on_the_repo():
    """R2-6: the copies, their constants and their default root equal the originals', which this test imports and
    core/oddsdata/inputs.py never does."""
    from core.ficc import macro_artifacts as MA
    from core.quant import gate_ledger as GL
    rel = "core/oddsdata/inputs.py"
    targets = {f"{module}.{name}" if name else module for _node, module, names, _f
               in CG._imports(rel, ast.parse((ROOT / rel).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))) for name in names or ("",)}
    assert not [t for t in targets if t.startswith(("core.quant.gate_ledger", "core.ficc.macro_artifacts"))], targets
    assert inputs.UNVERSIONED == GL.UNVERSIONED and inputs.TREE_GLOBS == MA.TREE_GLOBS
    assert inputs.REPO == GL.REPO_ROOT == MA.REPO_ROOT == ROOT
    assert inputs.repo_anchor() == GL.repo_anchor() and inputs.tree_hash() == MA.tree_hash()


def test_the_provenance_copies_equal_the_originals_on_synthetic_roots():
    """No .git, a ref: HEAD (loose, packed-refs only, neither), a detached sha, a non-hex HEAD, an unreadable HEAD;
    a small tree with files inside and outside TREE_GLOBS."""
    from core.ficc import macro_artifacts as MA
    from core.quant import gate_ledger as GL
    root = Path(os.environ["TRADEGEN_HOME"]) / "synthetic_repo"
    git = root / ".git"
    root.mkdir()

    def anchor(want: str) -> None:
        got = inputs.repo_anchor(root)
        assert got == GL.repo_anchor(root) == want, (got, GL.repo_anchor(root), want)
    anchor("UNVERSIONED")
    (git / "refs" / "heads").mkdir(parents=True)
    (git / "HEAD").write_text("ref: refs/heads/main\n", encoding="utf-8")
    anchor("UNVERSIONED")                                           # no loose ref and no packed-refs
    (git / "packed-refs").write_text(f"# pack-refs with: peeled\n{'c' * 40} refs/heads/other\n"
                                     f"{'d' * 40} refs/heads/main\n", encoding="utf-8")
    anchor("git:" + "d" * 40)
    (git / "refs" / "heads" / "main").write_text("a" * 40 + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    anchor("git:" + "a" * 40)                                       # the loose ref wins
    (git / "HEAD").write_text("b" * 40, encoding="utf-8")
    anchor("git:" + "b" * 40)                                       # detached
    (git / "HEAD").write_text("not a sha\n", encoding="utf-8")
    anchor("UNVERSIONED")
    (git / "HEAD").unlink()
    (git / "HEAD").mkdir()
    anchor("UNVERSIONED")                                           # reading HEAD raises OSError
    (root / "core" / "x").mkdir(parents=True)
    (root / "core" / "x" / "a.py").write_bytes(b"x = 1\r\n")
    (root / "core" / "b.py").write_bytes(b"")
    (root / "data" / "macro" / "sub").mkdir(parents=True)
    (root / "data" / "macro" / "f.yaml").write_bytes(b"k: v\n")
    (root / "data" / "macro" / "sub" / "g.bin").write_bytes(bytes(range(256)))
    (root / "config.py").write_bytes(b"A = 1\n")
    first = inputs.tree_hash(root)
    assert first == MA.tree_hash(root) and re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{64}", first), first
    (root / "core" / "notes.txt").write_bytes(b"outside the globs")
    (root / "data" / "other.yaml").write_bytes(b"outside the globs")
    assert inputs.tree_hash(root) == MA.tree_hash(root) == first
    (root / "data" / "macro" / "h.yaml").write_bytes(b"inside")
    assert inputs.tree_hash(root) == MA.tree_hash(root) != first
    (root / "empty").mkdir()
    assert inputs.tree_hash(root / "empty") == MA.tree_hash(root / "empty") == hashlib.sha256().hexdigest()


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# The comparison state (O12, Q12, Q34, Q36)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def test_begin_run_numbers_comparisons_and_keeps_each_ones_run():
    """Q12: new comparisons are c000001, c000002, ...; runs grows on every call; an issued id keeps its own run
    counter, so every invocation of it returns the same (id, run counter), the comparison's two inputs to the market
    seed (Q34), while K and J accumulate under it; R counts the comparisons that hold each plan hash."""
    assert inputs.begin_run(None, [H1], []) == ("c000001", 1, 1, 0, {H1: 1})
    assert inputs.begin_run(None, [H2, H1], [0.55]) == ("c000002", 2, 2, 1, {H2: 1, H1: 2})
    first = inputs.begin_run("c000001", [H2], [0.6])
    second = inputs.begin_run("c000001", [H2], [0.6])
    assert first == second == ("c000001", 1, 2, 1, {H2: 2}), (first, second)
    assert inputs.begin_run("c000001", [H3], [0.65]) == ("c000001", 1, 3, 2, {H3: 1})
    path = inputs.state_path()
    raw = path.read_bytes()
    doc = json.loads(raw)
    assert doc == {"schema": "tradegen.odds_state/1", "runs": 5, "comparisons": {
        "c000001": {"run": 1, "plans": [H1, H2, H3], "typed": [0.6, 0.65]},
        "c000002": {"run": 2, "plans": [H1, H2], "typed": [0.55]}}}, doc
    assert raw == (model.canonical_json(doc) + "\n").encode("utf-8") and not path.with_name("state.json.tmp").exists()
    assert inputs.begin_run(None, [H1], []) == ("c000006", 6, 1, 0, {H1: 3})     # a new comparison, a new counter


def test_begin_run_refuses_unknown_and_malformed_ids_writing_nothing():
    path = inputs.state_path()
    _raises(lambda: inputs.begin_run("c000001", [H1], []), ValueError)     # never issued: nothing exists yet
    assert not path.exists() and not path.parent.exists()
    inputs.begin_run(None, [H1], [])
    before = path.read_bytes()
    for comparison, hashes, typed in (("c000002", [H1], []), ("c1", [H1], []), ("C000001", [H1], []),
                                      ("c0000001", [H1], []), ("c000001\n", [H1], []), (1, [H1], []),
                                      (None, ["abc"], []), (None, ["F" * 64], []), (None, [H1], [math.nan]),
                                      (None, [H1], [True]), (None, [H1], ["0.5"])):
        _raises(lambda: inputs.begin_run(comparison, hashes, typed), ValueError)
        assert path.read_bytes() == before, (comparison, hashes, typed)


def test_begin_run_fails_closed_on_a_bad_state_file():
    """Q36: a state file that does not parse, has another schema, or holds a comparison without its own "run" (the
    earlier layout), with a run past `runs`, or under an id other than c<its run:06d> (after a hand-lowered `runs`, the
    next new id would be one already issued) is RuntimeError, and is never rewritten."""
    path = inputs.state_path()
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True)
    good = {"schema": inputs.STATE_SCHEMA, "runs": 1, "comparisons": {"c000001": {"run": 1, "plans": [H1],
                                                                                   "typed": []}}}
    bad = [b"not json\n", b"\xff\xfe\n", b"[]\n"]
    for change in ({"schema": "tradegen.odds_state/0"}, {"runs": "1"}, {"runs": True}, {"comparisons": []},
                   {"extra": 1}, {"comparisons": {"c000001": {"plans": [H1], "typed": []}}},
                   {"comparisons": {"c000002": {"run": 2, "plans": [H1], "typed": []}}},
                   {"runs": 2, "comparisons": {"c000003": {"run": 1, "plans": [H1], "typed": []}}},
                   {"comparisons": {"c000001": {"run": 1, "plans": [H2, H1], "typed": []}}},
                   {"comparisons": {"c1": {"run": 1, "plans": [H1], "typed": []}}}):
        bad.append((model.canonical_json({**good, **change}) + "\n").encode("utf-8"))
    for raw in bad:
        path.write_bytes(raw)
        _raises(lambda: inputs.begin_run(None, [H1], []), RuntimeError)
        assert path.read_bytes() == raw, raw
    path.write_bytes((model.canonical_json(good) + "\n").encode("utf-8"))
    assert inputs.begin_run("c000001", [H2], []) == ("c000001", 1, 2, 0, {H2: 1})    # the control parses


def test_begin_run_writes_through_checked_target():
    """A0: state_path() runs state_root()'s link scan first, on a clean temp home (memoised), so each refusal below
    comes from begin_run's own checked_target calls: a hard-linked state file is never rewritten, and an odds folder
    that became a junction after that scan is never written through."""
    import _winapi
    path = inputs.state_path()
    inputs.begin_run(None, [H1], [])
    os.link(path, path.with_name("second_name.json"))
    before = path.read_bytes()
    err = _raises(lambda: inputs.begin_run(None, [H1], []), RuntimeError)
    assert "writing it would change another file" in str(err), err
    assert path.read_bytes() == before
    for name in ("second_name.json", "state.json"):
        path.with_name(name).unlink()
    path.parent.rmdir()
    elsewhere = path.parent.with_name("elsewhere")
    elsewhere.mkdir()
    _winapi.CreateJunction(str(elsewhere), str(path.parent))
    err = _raises(lambda: inputs.begin_run(None, [H1], []), RuntimeError)
    assert "is a symlink or junction" in str(err) and not any(elsewhere.iterdir()), err


def test_build_inputs_fills_every_field():
    plan = _plan()
    series = P.Series(symbol="KRW-BTC", source="UPBIT", dates=("2026-10-22", "2026-10-23"), open=(1.0, 2.0),

                      md5=P.series_md5("KRW-BTC", "UPBIT", ("2026-10-22", "2026-10-23"), (1.0, 2.0), (1.5, 2.5), "",
                                       "final"))

def test_the_state_path_stays_under_the_tradegen_home():
    """The odds twin of macro_m0_rules.test_every_state_path_stays_out_of_quantgen for state.json."""
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

  Create `core/oddsdata/inputs.py` (whole file, LF):

```python
"""Unsigned inputs of the odds engine besides the bars (spec 4 "Calendars", "Provenance", 7.3 "Seeds"; O1, O6, O12;
R2-6; Q6, Q12, Q22, Q34, Q36).

The calendar set comes only from the owner's approved store, and only when owner.calendar_in_force names it and the
stored copy, with the files sessions() reads already loaded from it, still hashes to that name; the horizon's
sessions and dated KRX price limits are read from that set with `cal=` on every call, never from core.calendars'
default set. The session rules of its `calendars` config block (the KR Saturday-session cut-off, the close times)
come from the shipped rules store, which tree_hash records and the calendar sha does not cover (O1: the session list
is computed by unsigned code). `repo_anchor` and `tree_hash` are copies of core.quant.gate_ledger.repo_anchor and
core.ficc.macro_artifacts.tree_hash (R2-6: this package imports neither; tests/odds_inputs.py pins each copy to its
original). The comparison state lives in state_root()/odds/state.json, written atomically through checked_target; a
file that does not parse fails closed and the owner deletes it."""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import importlib.metadata
import json
import math
import os
import re
from datetime import date, datetime, timedelta
from pathlib import Path

from core.calendars import clocks, regime
from core.calendars.store import CalendarCoverageError, CalendarSet, CalendarUnsigned
from core.compliance import model, owner, rules
from core.isolation import checked_target, state_root
from core.odds import plan as P

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
UNVERSIONED = "UNVERSIONED"                                    # == core.quant.gate_ledger.UNVERSIONED
TREE_GLOBS = ("core/**/*.py", "data/macro/**/*", "config.py")  # == core.ficc.macro_artifacts.TREE_GLOBS
STATE_SCHEMA = "tradegen.odds_state/1"
CID_RE = r"c[0-9]{6}"
_MD5_FILES = {"KR": ("holidays_KRX", "kr_regime_tags", "kr_sessions"), "US": ("holidays_NYSE",)}


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Calendar and sessions (Q6, Q22)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def calendar_for(now: datetime) -> tuple[CalendarSet | None, str, str]:
    """(set, sha, error): the calendar set the owner approved and that is in force at `now`, read from the owner's
    store; (None, "", "unsigned: ...") when there is none or the stored copy no longer hashes to its approval. The
    files sessions() reads are loaded before that hash, so an edit made after it is never read."""
    sha = owner.calendar_in_force(now)
    if sha is None:
        return None, "", "unsigned: no signed calendar approval"
    folder = owner.store_dir() / "calendar" / sha
    cal = CalendarSet(folder)
    try:
        for fid in sorted({f for files in _MD5_FILES.values() for f in files}):
            cal.refusal(fid)                   # loads and caches the file, or its refusal, with the manifest
        intact = rules.calendar_sha256(folder) == sha
    except (OSError, rules.Invalid):
        intact = False
    if not intact:
        return None, "", "unsigned: the stored calendar set does not hash to its approval"
    return cal, sha, ""


def sessions(market: str, start: date, horizon_days: int, cal: CalendarSet | None
             ) -> tuple[tuple[str, ...], tuple[float, ...], tuple[tuple[str, str], ...], str, str]:
    """(dates, KRX price limits, (file id, md5) pairs, calendar version, error) of the half-open horizon
    [start, start + horizon_days). CRYPTO: every date, no calendar. KR and US: the sessions of `cal` (KR with the
    price limit in force on each date); a missing or unsigned set gives "unsigned: ...", a horizon outside its
    coverage "coverage: ...", both with no dates."""
    if market == "CRYPTO":
        return tuple((start + timedelta(days=i)).isoformat() for i in range(horizon_days)), (), (), "", ""
    if market not in _MD5_FILES:
        raise ValueError(f"sessions: market {market!r} is not KR, US or CRYPTO")
    if cal is None:
        return (), (), (), "", "unsigned: no signed calendar set"
    try:
        found = clocks.sessions_between(market, start, start + timedelta(days=horizon_days - 1), cal=cal)
        limits = tuple(float(regime.regime_tags("KR", d, cal=cal)["price_limit"]) for d in found) \
            if market == "KR" else ()
        md5s = tuple((fid, cal.file(fid).md5) for fid in _MD5_FILES[market])
        version = cal.version
    except CalendarUnsigned as exc:
        return (), (), (), "", f"unsigned: {exc}"
    except CalendarCoverageError as exc:
        return (), (), (), "", f"coverage: {exc}"
    return tuple(d.isoformat() for d in found), limits, md5s, version, ""


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# Provenance (R2-6): copies of gate_ledger.repo_anchor and macro_artifacts.tree_hash
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def repo_anchor(root: Path = REPO) -> str:
    """`git:<sha>` of HEAD when the folder is a git repository, else UNVERSIONED (copy of gate_ledger's)."""
    head = Path(root) / ".git" / "HEAD"
    try:
        text = head.read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip()
        if text.startswith("ref:"):
            ref = text[4:].strip()
            loose = Path(root) / ".git" / ref
            if loose.is_file():
                text = loose.read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip()
            else:                                   # after `git gc` / `git pack-refs` the ref lives in packed-refs only
                packed = (Path(root) / ".git" / "packed-refs").read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
                text = next((ln.split()[0] for ln in packed if ln.endswith(" " + ref)), "")
        return f"git:{text}" if re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{40}", text) else UNVERSIONED
    except OSError:
        return UNVERSIONED


def tree_hash(root: Path = REPO) -> str:
    """sha256 over sorted relative paths + bytes of core/**/*.py, data/macro/**, config.py (macro_artifacts' copy)."""
    root = Path(root)
    files = sorted({p for g in TREE_GLOBS for p in root.glob(g) if p.is_file()},
                   key=lambda p: p.relative_to(root).as_posix())
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    for p in files:
        h.update(p.relative_to(root).as_posix().encode("utf-8") + b"\0" + p.read_bytes() + b"\0")
    return h.hexdigest()


def provenance() -> P.Provenance:
    """The repo anchor, the tree hash and the installed cryptography version ("absent" when it is not installed)."""
    try:
        crypto = importlib.metadata.version("cryptography")
    except importlib.metadata.PackageNotFoundError:
        crypto = "absent"
    return P.Provenance(repo_anchor=repo_anchor(), tree_hash=tree_hash(), cryptography=crypto)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
# The comparison state (Q12, Q34, Q36)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
def state_path() -> Path:
    return state_root() / "odds" / "state.json"


def _number(v) -> bool:
    return isinstance(v, (int, float)) and not isinstance(v, bool) and math.isfinite(v)


def _hex64(v) -> bool:
    return isinstance(v, str) and re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{64}", v) is not None


def _state_ok(doc) -> bool:
    """A tradegen.odds_state/1 document: every comparison holds its own run counter (1 <= run <= runs, its id
    c<run:06d>, so ids and runs are unique and a new id is never an issued one), sorted unique plan hashes and sorted
    unique typed rates."""
    if not (isinstance(doc, dict) and set(doc) == {"schema", "runs", "comparisons"} and doc["schema"] == STATE_SCHEMA
            and isinstance(doc["runs"], int) and not isinstance(doc["runs"], bool) and doc["runs"] >= 0
            and isinstance(doc["comparisons"], dict)):
        return False
    for cid, comp in doc["comparisons"].items():
        if not (re.fullmatch(CID_RE, cid) and isinstance(comp, dict) and set(comp) == {"run", "plans", "typed"}
                and isinstance(comp["run"], int) and not isinstance(comp["run"], bool)
                and 1 <= comp["run"] <= doc["runs"] and cid == f"c{comp['run']:06d}"
                and isinstance(comp["plans"], list)
                and all(_hex64(h) for h in comp["plans"]) and comp["plans"] == sorted(set(comp["plans"]))
                and isinstance(comp["typed"], list) and all(_number(p) for p in comp["typed"])
                and comp["typed"] == sorted(set(comp["typed"]))):
            return False
    return True


def _read_state(path: Path) -> dict:
    if not path.exists():
        return {"schema": STATE_SCHEMA, "runs": 0, "comparisons": {}}
    try:
        doc = json.loads(path.read_bytes().decode("utf-8"))
    except (UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError):
        doc = None
    if not _state_ok(doc):
        raise RuntimeError(f"odds state {path}: not a {STATE_SCHEMA} file; the owner deletes it before the next run")
    return doc


def begin_run(comparison: str | None, plan_hashes: list[str], typed: list[float]
              ) -> tuple[str, int, int, int, dict[str, int]]:
    """Opens one run: a new comparison (comparison None, id c<runs:06d>, its run counter fixed at creation) or an
    issued one (its own counter reused, so every invocation of it gets the same seed). Adds the plan hashes and typed
    win rates, writes the state atomically, and returns (id, run counter, K plans, J typed rates, R per plan hash:
    the number of comparisons whose plans hold it). ValueError, writing nothing, for an id that is malformed or was
    never issued, or a plan hash or rate that is not one."""
    # ponytail: one writer at a time. Two overlapping runs read the same `runs`, issue the same new id and counter
    # (one seed), and the later os.replace drops the other's plans; take an exclusive state.lock (open "x" after
    # checked_target) if runs can ever overlap. Ids stop at c999999: run 1,000,000 writes c1000000, which the next
    # read refuses; widen CID_RE before that.
    if comparison is not None and not (isinstance(comparison, str) and re.fullmatch(CID_RE, comparison)):
        raise ValueError(f"comparison id {comparison!r} is not c followed by six digits")
    if not all(_hex64(h) for h in plan_hashes) or not all(_number(p) for p in typed):
        raise ValueError("begin_run: plan hashes are 64 hex characters and typed rates finite numbers")
    path = state_path()
    state = _read_state(path)
    comps = state["comparisons"]
    if comparison is not None and comparison not in comps:
        raise ValueError(f"comparison {comparison} was never issued; leave --comparison out to start a new one")
    state["runs"] += 1
    cid = comparison or f"c{state['runs']:06d}"
    comp = comps.setdefault(cid, {"run": state["runs"], "plans": [], "typed": []})
    comp["plans"] = sorted(set(comp["plans"]) | set(plan_hashes))
    comp["typed"] = sorted(set(comp["typed"]) | {float(p) for p in typed})
    base = path.parent
    checked_target(base, "odds folder", within=state_root())     # a junction made after state_root()'s scan (A0)
    target = checked_target(path, "odds state", within=base)
    tmp = checked_target(base / "state.json.tmp", "odds state tmp", within=base)
    base.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    tmp.write_bytes((model.canonical_json(state) + "\n").encode("utf-8"))
    os.replace(tmp, target)
    seen = {h: sum(h in c["plans"] for c in comps.values()) for h in plan_hashes}
    return cid, comp["run"], len(comp["plans"]), len(comp["typed"]), seen


def build_inputs(plan, now: datetime, *, series, sessions_info, calendar_sha: str, replay, run) -> P.Inputs:
    """plan.Inputs from the pieces: `sessions_info` is the 5-tuple of sessions(), `run` the 5-tuple of begin_run()."""
    dates, limits, md5s, version, error = sessions_info
    cid, counter, k, j, seen = run
    return P.Inputs(now=now, series=series, sessions=dates, price_limits=limits, calendar_sha256=calendar_sha,
                    calendar_version=version, calendar_md5s=md5s, calendar_error=error, replay=replay,
                    comparison_id=cid, run_counter=counter, comparison_plans=k, comparison_typed=j,
                    plan_runs=seen[P.plan_hash(plan)], provenance=provenance())
```
